#4827. The 7 Best LED Face Masks for Men in 2026, According to Experts

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

For battling blemishes and signs of aging, there are few better at-home tools.

AS SOMEONE RAISED on slasher horror movies, I was always going to gravitate towards LED face masks. But while their creepy Jason Voorhees-at-a-rave look is what initially grabbed my attention, the skincare benefits are what sold me on the products. LED face masks combine the firming power of anti-aging products, the depuffing of eye cream, the energizing boost of moisturizers, and the breakout-fighting strength of acne washes—making them one of the most versatile grooming tools out there.

LED masks use specific wavelengths of light to penetrate the skin and trigger cellular changes, according to dermatologist Dr. Hannah Kopelman, MD. This can include stimulating collagen production to reduce fine lines and support firmer skin, as well as treating acne-causing bacteria and calming inflammation to promote a clearer complexion. Some devices offer all of these benefits, while others are laser-focused (get it?) on just one or two. The key is to know what each is capable of and what service you’re looking for.

Dermatologist Dr. Brian Toy, MD, warns that the market is flooded with LED face masks that vary greatly in quality and effectiveness, so it’s best to start your search as informed as possible. To temper the confusion, I went ahead and used myself, along with fellow Men’s Health writers and editors, as guinea pigs. This way, you’ll know what works and what is merely an overpriced Halloween mask.

We gave Shark Beauty CryoGlow a 2025 Men’s Health Grooming Award barely a month after it was released; that’s how great this LED mask is. It offers four separate treatment options that cover anything you could possibly want out of an LED face mask. The Better Aging setting uses red and infrared light to reduce wrinkles and firm skin, while Skin Clearing mode combines blue, red, and infrared light to fight blemishes and even tone.

The Skin Sustain maintains glow with a quick mix of all three LED wavelengths, and Under-Eye Revive uses cryotherapy-inspired cooling to depuff and tighten the under-eye area. You can also use this under-eye cooling ability combined with the other treatments, which roll out in three increasing levels of chill. Each is between four and eight minutes, meaning you don’t need to dedicate much time to combat whatever issue you’re after. Under-Eye Revive, you can do up to 15 minutes if you’d like, but you only need five to be effective.

Dr. Peterson Pierre, MD, FAAD, likes that this device uses red, blue, and infrared lights so that you can get a full smorgasbord of benefits, like combating acne, fighting signs of aging, reducing inflammation, and helping regulate oil production. He also digs the cooling feature and three levels of intensity. I’ve been using my CryoGlow for months, and have seen a noticeable change in the smoothness and clearness of my skin, as well as reduced redness, using The Better Aging and Skin Clearing settings. But where I saw the most immediate results was with eye puffiness.

If I’m ever running on limited sleep or recovering from a night out, I pop the mask on, and after a few minutes of Under-Eye Revive mode, I look like I’ve actually slept. The light from this device doesn’t feel glaring when you’re wearing it, so I was able to successfully walk around and multitask during my treatments.

Plus, as someone who is generally sensitive to light, it also feels a lot less intense than other options on this list, and never inspired headaches of any kind. Not to mention, it’s easy to adjust and fits my face perfectly. I only have a few nitpicks. Given the expansive options and customizability of this mask, there is a handheld controller attached to it to help you navigate. While this makes firing up the device super easy and you don’t need to rely on an app, the controller can be a bit awkward to deal with while you’re in treatment.

You can’t put it in your pocket without accidentally changing the setting, so you have to hold it, which limits the multitasking you’re able to do. Also, the mask is bulkier than its main competition for best overall, the Dr. Dennis Gross Face Mask. But when you consider that the CryoGlow is also the cheapest full-face option on this list, it’s a fair trade-off.

Read More: Shark CryoGlow LED Face Mask Review

Dr. Kopelman has been recommending this LED mask to patients for years. She likes that it is FDA-cleared and offers both red and blue light; however, what she likes most about it is that it consistently delivers results. In terms of effectiveness, it’s equal to the CryoGlow. The only reason it just missed out on the top spot is that it’s over $100 more expensive and offers fewer additional treatments, like under-eye cooling. Beyond that, I find it just as successful at battling blemishes and signs of aging as the Shark Beauty.

Plus, the treatments are shorter, and you only need to wear this for three minutes a day to see results. Unlike many other options, like the CurrentBody or FAQ 202, which are made of more flexible material you can mold to your face, this design is rigid. While that may seem like a drawback, I loved it. Of all the LED masks on this list, I found Dr. Dennis Gross to be the sturdiest, and it fit my face perfectly. It’s slim, without feeling flimsy, and doesn’t weigh down my face like other similarly sturdy masks that tend to be a bit heavier, such as the Theraface Mask.

That being said, I possess an incredibly average build and face shape, so if you fall outside of those parameters, the singular and unadaptable design of this mask might not be as perfect a fit. Unlike the CryoGlow, it’s wireless when you’re using it and can be conveniently charged with any USB-C charger. This helps when traveling, though the solid design poses some challenges if you’re tight on storage space.

Similar to the Dr. Dennis Gross mask, this device is crafted with a hard, contoured shell; however, it’s far less slim. But it trades off this added bulkiness with its vibrating ability, which soothes facial tension and boosts blood flow around the eyes, brows, and scalp. It offers red, blue, and infrared light therapy to target acne, improve skin tone, and increase collagen production.

You can choose between three- or nine-minute treatment modes, though we found the longer sessions to be more effective. Sure, this mask can feel a bit heavy or bulky on the face, but the results are legit. In fact, some effects can be seen immediately, and they only increase from there. “After the very first time I used it, my skin felt softer, and my pores looked smaller,” says Senior Gear and Commerce Editor Ryan Brower.

“Over time, my skin tone looks more even, and my skin appears to be firmer, smoother, and less puffy.” He adds that the massaging, vibrating feature is relaxing, although it can feel ticklish or even chill-inducing at times. Since it sits close to your ears, it can also get a bit loud, especially when multitasking. Still, it’s really easy to switch between settings, turn on and off, and choose the massage style you want.

If you’re solely looking to combat puffiness, dark circles, and wrinkles, Lumin is the way to go. Sure, it looks straight out of an abandoned Lone Ranger In Space reboot, but there is no device better at rejuvenating the skin around the eyes than this mask. One tester saw noticeable improvements after days of use with this device. “I naturally have darker circles, but after consistent daily use for about a week, I saw a noticeable difference in the brightness and overall alertness of my eye area,” she says. The mask stays in place well, and the soft silicone padding makes it comfortable throughout each session.

Its adjustable design also ensures it fits all face shapes and sizes with ease. The same tester also saw a brighter tone and smoother skin after a couple of weeks of daily use. “While I don’t personally have under-eye wrinkles, I can see how this would be especially helpful for someone who does or for anyone who spends a lot of time in the sun,” she says. Not to mention, the Luminator is quick and easy to use—just three minutes a day with an auto timer.

Our testers found that this FAQ mask makes a strong impression right out of the box with its ultra-thin, flexible design, which feels more like a high-end sheet mask than a tech device. You’ll need to download the app to get the most out of this tool, however. There’s a single button on the mask, but without the app, we found that it was nearly impossible to remember its function or how to power it off.

Once the app is set up and the mask is synced, navigating the features becomes straightforward—just select your desired treatment and that’s it. Despite being covered in tiny LED lights, the mask feels surprisingly lightweight and comfortable. During the 15-minute session, testers reported no heat or noticeable sensation on the skin and even forgot it was on while doing other tasks, such as reading. The mask stays comfortably in place, even when looking down at a book or phone.

We also appreciated the included cleaning spray. For anyone with sensitive or breakout-prone skin, keeping the mask clean is essential, and the spray makes that simple. After each use, we cleaned and dried the mask before placing it in its pouch, which securely holds the device and makes storage hassle-free. One minor concern was the split at the bridge of the nose—designed for flexibility—which left one tester wondering if that area was receiving full treatment. Still, this didn’t deter them from continuing to use it.

Women’s Health fitness contributor Nicolette Accardi says that the Qure Pro LED Mask has taken her nightly skincare regimen to the next level. After a month of use, she saw a dramatic difference in her skin’s appearance. She used to struggle with oily skin and frequent breakouts, but since regularly using the pink LED light setting, she says it has significantly reduced her sebum production. “I'm also approaching 30 (yikes), so I've been using the red LED light setting as well to help combat fine lines and reverse skin aging,” Accardi says.

Each session runs for three minutes and automatically shuts off when it’s done, so you never have to worry about timing it yourself. It’s perfect for anyone who wants results without the hassle. It’s one of the easiest, most low-maintenance skincare tools out there at a relatively low cost. That’s not to say $380 is cheap, but when it comes to legit, effective LED masks, you won’t find many other options under $400. It’s really just this and the CryoGlow.

If the more rigid masks, like CryoGlow, Qure, and Dr. Dennis Gross, are too bulky for you, but the FAQ is too small for your face, Currentbody will be your best option. This mask offers the most flexibility, with a silicone design that easily molds to the contours of any face, ensuring full coverage. This is as long as you tighten the straps. I’ve been lazy a few times with that, and it will start slipping off your face mid-treatment. In addition to the flexible fit, this mask feels super gentle on the face.

One of our testers used it only days after getting eye surgery with no issue. Didn’t bother her eyes one bit. That being said, it takes up to six hours for a full charge, which can be a bit annoying. This is the longest charge time on this list by a few hours, to be clear. I’m the type of person who pushes off charging a device until I absolutely have to, so this long charge time usually results in me skipping a day of treatment. But if you’re a better planner (to be fair, it’s a low bar compared to me), it’ll be less of an issue.

Depending on what skin issues or concerns you’re looking to address with your LED face mask, you’ll want to focus on which treatments it offers. This is driven by the color of light the device uses, which dictates its benefits. Some on this list offer multiple services, while others zero in on one. These are the common options:

While some are comfortable and allow for multitasking, there is no getting around the fact that you’re wearing a large light on your face. As a long-time migraine sufferer, having a light this close to my eyes for too long can be a trigger. But even if you’re perfectly fine with prolonged light exposure, you’ll want to know what the time commitment is before buying LED face masks, as they’re most effective when used regularly. Some are as long as 25 minutes, while others can be as short as three minutes. Keep in mind that not all are meant for everyday use; some (especially the ones with longer treatment lengths) may only need to be used a few times a week for max efficiency.

When shopping for an LED face mask, choosing a device that’s FDA-cleared is essential, says Dr. Kopelman. This ensures the product meets fundamental safety standards for consumer use. To be clear, however, FDA-cleared is not the same as FDA-approved—the latter involves extensive clinical trials and rigorous testing. Currently, no LED face masks on the market have achieved FDA approval.

For now, stick with FDA-cleared options, which means the device is proven to be as safe and effective as another legally marketed product. You might also see terms like FDA-registered or FDA-listed, but these simply indicate that the manufacturer has notified the FDA of the product's existence—there’s no review or evaluation involved. Because of that uncertainty, you won’t see any of those on this list.

There are a lot of LED face masks out there, and like any trendy tool, not all are created equal. So, before putting any to the test, I consulted with a panel of dermatologists on which devices were legit and which they recommend. They also advised me on what to look for in a quality LED face mask and the brands to focus on. Based on this intel, I, along with other Men’s Health writers and editors, put several masks to the test, evaluating each device’s effectiveness, ease of use, and how comfortable it was to wear.

As many LED face masks do not offer immediate results, we used each one for at least one month to ensure enough time was given to gain any possible benefits. Following this extensive research and testing, I landed on these seven LED face masks as the best for men in 2026.

The dermatologists I spoke to for this story were clear on this: you should be cleaning your device after every use. If you don’t, bacteria, oil, and product residue can build up on the surface and transfer back onto your skin, causing irritation or breakouts, which may ironically be what you were hoping to minimize by using an LED mask in the first place.

Dr. Kopelman says that LED masks should always be used on freshly cleansed, dry skin to ensure the light penetrates as effectively as possible. After the session, apply your serums and moisturizers—doing it beforehand can block the light and reduce its benefits. A hydrating serum like hyaluronic acid or a peptide-rich cream works especially well to complement the collagen boost from the treatment, Dr. Kopelman says.

According to Dr. Toy, be sure to skip any products that might react to light. For example, because retinol and vitamin C serums are photosensitizing, they’re an absolute no-go before any LED treatment. Dr. Chacon adds that reflective products like heavy oils or sunscreens should also be avoided during use as they can scatter the light and disrupt the device’s effectiveness.

#4826. Honda’s $2,000 electric moped is a winner. So why can’t Americans buy it?

Honda has been steadily expanding its electric motorcycle lineup, but one of its most interesting new models isn’t a flashy high-performance machine. It’s a modest little electric scooter called the Honda UC3, and with prices now dipping close to $2,000 in local markets, it’s the kind of affordable electric two-wheeler that many Americans would probably love to get their hands on.

Unfortunately, that’s probably not happening anytime soon.

We first covered the Honda UC3 earlier this year when the company announced plans to launch the electric scooter in Thailand and Vietnam. Designed as an electric equivalent to a 110cc gasoline-powered scooter, the UC3 is built for practical everyday transportation rather than weekend joyrides.

But don’t let its modest appearance fool you. The UC3 packs a 6 kW (8 hp) electric motor capable of reaching approximately 50 mph (80 km/h), making it more than capable of handling typical urban commuting.

Its 3.2 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery provides up to 76 miles (122 km) of range under WMTC testing. Unlike Honda’s other electric scooters that use removable batteries, the UC3 has a permanently installed battery that charges directly on the bike.

There’s also a full-color TFT display, smartphone connectivity, three riding modes, reverse gear, and a generous 26-liter under-seat storage compartment.

And perhaps most importantly, it comes from Honda, a company with decades of experience building reliable, affordable motorcycles.

The UC3 originally launched in Vietnam with prices starting around 78.5 million Vietnamese dong, or roughly $3,000. However, recent reports from Vietnamese dealerships show incentives bringing prices down to around 54 million dong, equivalent to approximately $2,100.

That’s a pretty compelling price for a 50 mph (80 km/h) electric scooter from one of the world’s largest motorcycle manufacturers.

But despite its appeal, Honda hasn’t announced any plans to bring the UC3 to the United States.

In much of Southeast Asia, scooters are everyday transportation, with millions of riders using them for commuting, shopping, and practically everything else. In the US, motorcycles are much more commonly recreational vehicles, and the market for small, practical scooters is comparatively tiny.

I'm hoping scooters like this take over the world, the sooner the better. Anyone who's travelled in any cities in Asian, India, or most of Europe, there's always a constant background whine of 2-stroke scooters, day and night.

I would have thought these kinds of markets would have already transitioned to EV - in addition to the annoying sound, those 2-stroke engines spew out an order of magnitude more pollution than most ICE vehicles. I guess it's been a cost issue - this scooter should be cheap enough to take over the world.

Add in the costs of US regulatory certification, establishing parts and service support, and navigating a market where many buyers expect motorcycles to handle highway speeds, and the business case becomes considerably less attractive.

That’s unfortunate, because the UC3 looks like exactly the kind of electric two-wheeler that could make a real difference in American cities.

It’s affordable, practical, fast enough for most city streets, and backed by a manufacturer that isn’t going anywhere.

Now if only Honda would give Americans a chance to buy one.

It’s a cheeky comment about the beaming hue she herself chose for clients in the Berkshires—a color that defines their entire lakeside home, one she calls the diva of the whole project, requiring (no, demanding) decisions in every square foot to balance out its intensity.

Cooney’s clients didn’t blink at the bold idea. Unusually carefree for a couple with high-powered jobs, they gave the AD PRO Directory designer free license to create. The bungalow was purchased as a weekend retreat from life in New York, but even before paint swatches were discussed, the kitchen was a sticking point. “The kitchen was crazy—it was this tiny little makeshift kitchen,” says Cooney.

Cooney’s clients weren’t initially convinced by reclaimed brick flooring in the entryway, but Cooney’s team proved convincing—they believed the space needed a worn palette to counterbalance the intensely yellow kitchen. Much to their clients’ delight, it worked beautifully. A Croft House Morro Credenza with leather-front doors anchors the space, topped with a vintage lamp from Millerton Antiques Center and set beneath an unknown artwork from Brimfield Flea Market.

Cooney opted to stain wood-paneled walls in custom blue and brown stains from Rubio Monocoat, allowing rustic grains to shine through. Atop a Jaipur Hazan rug, an upholstered George Smith Emma Ottoman anchors the room and is accompanied by a set of armchairs and a velvet mordoré sofa from Lawson-Fenning. A 20th-century oil painting by Paul Berg hangs above the reworked fireplace, while in the corner, above a Charles Dudouyt side table, hangs a vintage painting sourced from The Little Store in Massachusetts.

“We just decided to kind of lean into it and go almost in a maximalist way,” says Cooney of the dining room’s focal point, a painting by K.G. Narendra Babu that inspired the home’s many colors. For the inside of a Four Hands Camila Sideboard, they commissioned artisan Joel Haynes to hand-paint a leafy pattern. A Hubbardton Forge Disq fixture hangs above a custom Bossi dining table surrounded with Tribute Modern Dining Chairs from Craft Associates.

The husband, an English lawyer, craved a small cabin in the woods, while the wife, an Italian who loves cooking, wanted a home large enough to host intimate gatherings. “This house was a happy compromise,” says the husband. But while the home spans three levels and around 4,500 square feet, the main floor measured just about 1,000. The kitchen, in a cramped corner, didn’t cut it

Cooney’s team reconfigured a few walls. They collapsed oversized closets in the entryway, shrinking the space to a slimmer mudroom while letting the entire layout exhale, expanding the footprint of the semi-open cooking area. The room is now the proper heart of the home, and its bright yellow cabinets aren’t shy about it.

Cabinets with glass windows were fabricated by Westek Architectural Woodworking and feature an array of white porcelain that punctuates and calms the intensely painted millwork; the pieces were all sourced from shops in the Berkshires, including Millerton Antiques, All that Jazz, and Montage Antiques.

“It’s the diva of the project,” says Cooney of the yellow Benjamin Moore paint used throughout the kitchen, a choice that influenced nearly all palettes throughout the home. Ceilings, walls, and upper cabinets were painted in Farrow & Ball’s New White.

The kitchen island is topped with a wooden counter and is paired with Amber Interiors Cade Counter Stools in walnut. A set of Matthew Fairbank Allegro Pendants hang above the island.

The saturated hue, Benjamin Moore’s Glen Ridge Gold, wasn’t a choice made on a whim. Like many colors peppering the home, it was inspired by a painting by Chennai-based artist K.G. Narendra Babu that now hangs in the couple’s dining room. The artwork was given to the couple by a family member who worked in India, and it features an array of folk and musical motifs.

“The whole point of the project is that it’s bright and energetic and deeply relaxing at the same time,” says Cooney. “That was the trust that they put in us—to believe that both could happen.”

The architecture itself lacked a definitive style. Light traces of Arts & Crafts style gave Cooney a point of view to reinvent existing character. A fireplace in the living room is now reimagined with glazed brick Clé tiles, their dappled surface cladding the surround with clean lines and a crafted look; a custom stain allowed wood-paneled walls to bear rustic grains but in modern blue-green tones.

To expand the kitchen’s footprint, Cooney reclaimed space from unnecessarily large closets in the entryway. Her team moved the wall to install smaller, but equally useful, cabinets that turn the space into a mudroom. The custom millwork, crafted by Westek Architectural Woodworking and painted in Farrow & Ball’s Blue Gray, complements a vintage rug and a built-in bench.

A custom walnut vanity injects warmth as an alternative to a colder stone. Cooney’s team used a boat sealer to coat and protect the walnut, giving the material a high-gloss finish. A fabric shade made with Eric Kuster’s Micha 002 textile occupies the space that might traditionally feature a mirror. “You can kind of break a rule and have it be playful and fun, especially in a powder bath,” says Cooney, noting that a mirror hangs on the side wall instead. The wallcovering is Pierre Frey’s Uberon print.

Cooney describes an almost cottagey feel in the primary, thanks to a walnut Flora Bed by Jacob May, which was locally made and turned by hand, layered with cozy and textural textiles like Parachute Home’s Hand Stitched Cotton Quilt. Gentle patterns add to the mix through a Scandinavian kilim with geometric design from Rug & Kilim, and light drapes made with a Best Buds textile by Kerry Joyce.

Making the most of existing features, light touches to the bathroom reimagined the space, like painting existing wainscoting in Farrow & Ball’s Tanner’s Brown, and covering the walls in a botanical House of Hackney Herbarium wallpaper. For a touch of texture, Cooney also layered vintage rugs and set an antique Victorian bamboo chair in the corner below the window.

With a view over the living room, Cooney says the lofted floor is like a little escape within the small cottage. Leaning into the cozy feel, the team went with a layered look. A brass chest anchors the space, paired with a black armchair owned by the clients, which was reupholstered with a burgundy fabric from Abraham Moon & Sons, and a Lawson-Fenning Morro Sectional in a linen blend.

The clients’ only real hesitation was a bit of a surprise: the reclaimed brick Cooney specified for the mudroom. It is laid in a herringbone pattern with colors that appeared to shift across the surface. That yellow kitchen? Totally fine. But the expressive bricks? Too dramatic. “We relied on the team’s judgement, and this feature is now one of our most favorite parts of the home,” says the husband, noting how guests often compliment the mudroom.

“I feel like this house is kind of us unchecked,” says Cooney of her clients’ trust. “No one checked us, so we were allowed to do the fullest extent of what we wanted to do.” Her clients could easily have staged their own diva moment after the cabinets were painted in screaming yellow, before everything else around it fell into place around it; but they let the vision come into full focus.

As if cantilevered over the hill, a screened-in porch is the best of both worlds. “You don’t have to have everything be indoor-outdoor in a covered porch—you can really pull the inside out there and not worry so much,” says Cooney, nodding to choices like Henning Kjaernulf dining chairs from the 1960s purchased from Lone Fox. And while most might use a lighter color in this space, Cooney chose a deeper Farrow & Ball Hopper Head paint for the walls and window frames, which she says helps punctuate the view in a beautiful way.

#4824. The Best Shampoos for Every Hair Need and Budget, According to Experts

From L’Oréal to Oribe, these shampoos are worthy of a spot in your wash day routine.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

From sweaty runs and heat styling to product buildup, our scalps and hair need proper TLC—and that starts with a great shampoo. Our scalp is an extension of the skin on our face—it sheds dead skin cells, collects dirt and bacteria, and secretes oil and sweat, says trichologist Anabel Kingsley in our guide on how often to shampoo your hair. While the beauty community has mixed opinions on the cadence of shampooing, dermatologist DiAnne Davis, MD, recommends doing so at least once a week. The frequency varies based on your lifestyle, how quickly your hair gets greasy, your scalp health, and hair type. Since the experts advise regular shampooing, I asked the pros about how we can upgrade our healthy hair routines to preserve the expensive chemical and color treatments we enjoy at the salon.

“I always tell my clients that shampoo is mainly for your scalp, so I would start there,” says trichologist and hairstylist Courtney Foster. “You can have curly hair with an oily scalp, fine hair with a dry scalp, or color-treated hair with buildup. Hair type matters, but it doesn't tell me everything I need to know.” Choose hydrating shampoos that nourish a dry scalp, or use a lightweight shampoo with fewer moisturizing ingredients for an oily scalp.

For an oily scalp or buildup, ingredients like salicylic acid can be helpful, along with gentle cleansing agents like coco glucoside. For mineral and hard water buildup, look for chelating ingredients, as regular shampoo alone may not remove these deposits, according to Foster.

Now it’s time to think about your hair type, advises Foster. In addition to your hair texture, you’ll want to find a shampoo that’s suitable for your dry, chemically treated, damaged, or breakage-prone mane.

For dryness, humectants and conditioning ingredients such as glycerin, hyaluronic acid, and nourishing oils are your new beauty best friends. They help the hair retain moisture and feel softer and more manageable, says Foster.

For damaged hair, you’ll need shampoos packed with amino acids and bond-strengthening ingredients. “These are good for hair that has been chemically treated or excessively heat-styled,” she says of components such as hydrolyzed proteins, which can improve the feel and strength of damaged hair.

Now, if you’re dealing with frizz like I am, it likely means the hair is lacking moisture, says Foster. We’ll benefit from conditioning ingredients like polymers, silicones, oils, and humectants that help smooth the cuticle and improve manageability.

As our hair-obsessed beauty editor, I own a sizable shampoo collection. It’s 24 shampoos strong. So I started there and narrowed it down to 12 contenders. In addition to expert guidance—ingredients for a healthy scalp and cosmetic concerns like frizz—I factored in everything from their cleansing power, lather, fragrance, and feel. Did they leave my scalp parched like I just went swimming in the pool? Or did they help rebalance my scalp and prevent embarrassing flakes on my black clothing?

To help whittle down potential recommendations even further, I recruited the Women’s Health team, including beauty director Brian Underwood and deputy editor Carina Hsieh, to test these picks. Ouai Fine Hair Shampoo and Leonor Greyl immediately caught our attention and kept it. The latter even won a Women’s Health Beauty Award, and we don’t take giving out that accolade lightly.

Still, I wanted to tap into other expert picks and asked hairstylists and trichologists about the products they use at the salon and at home. Their suggestions range from a drugstore pick to a de-brassing shampoo to keep your color-treated hair looking as fresh as possible after washing.

While it sounds obvious, I factored in your budget. While my best overall pick from Oribe is on the higher end, there are several under $20 picks. And if your wallet is also looking a little tight during fun holiday adventures, I totally get it. We tested several of these shampoos, and each full-size bottle lasted us at least six weeks, with some lasting our team up to four months.

Ultimately, these are solid jumping-off points for your healthy hair routine. “One shampoo doesn’t necessarily have to do everything,” says Foster. If you use a lot of styling products, you may occasionally need a clarifying shampoo and a moisturizing shampoo for your regular wash days. “The goal is really to create a routine that keeps the scalp clean without stripping the hair.” Since you’re here, consider checking out our guides to healthy hair, including our favorite editor-tested hair masks, vitamins for hair growth, and red light therapy for hair growth. Yes, it’s a legitimate technology that’s backed by research, and dermatologists are on board.

I’d normally roll my eyes at anyone recommending a high-end shampoo as their best overall pick, but Oribe is the only shampoo I have on auto-refill. Despite its upfront cost, a single bottle of Oribe lasted me nearly four months, so it really helps stretch my cost per use.

My scalp has never been this clean with a single wash before. It helps wash away my silicone hair serum and dry shampoo buildup, and even sand from the Caribbean Sea that recently got stuck in my hair. It also softens my dry tresses before I even apply conditioner, which is incredible, given how parched my mane is.

Cleansing with Oribe really brings that luxurious feeling of being at the salon’s shampoo bowl from the comfort of my bathroom. Plus, it smells like Calabrian bergamot, white butterfly jasmine, and sandalwood. The blend is so enticing that Oribe even created a perfume inspired by this iconic scent. The chic black bottle pops in my otherwise boring gray bathroom.

And don’t just take my word for it: Foster appreciates that it combines gentle cleansers with conditioning ingredients, such as panthenol, amino acids, proteins, and oils. “It cleanses while still giving the hair a polished, conditioned feel,” she says.

You don’t need to splurge to enjoy a great shampoo, argues Foster. “L’Oréal gives you an elevated experience at the drugstore price point,” she says. “It produces a substantial lather and has more of a fragranced, salon-product feel than many inexpensive shampoos.” She especially likes it for anyone dealing with dryness or color-treated hair, or who wants a gentle daily shampoo without the luxury price tag.

“I love this product. It's available everywhere, which means I can travel light with just hand luggage and pick it up wherever I land,” says celebrity hairstylist and Kennaland salon owner Kenna Kennor. “The results are instantly better than most hotel shampoos.”

A combo of Cécred’s Bioactive keratin ferment and hyaluronic acid gently cleanses my hair while leaving it nourished and detangled, which is not exactly the norm for my dry curls. It works equally well on my natural hair and extensions, and it’s so gentle that you can use it on color-treated hair.

Foster especially likes this one for dry hair because it’s formulated with hydrating ingredients and is sulfate-free. “It is designed to provide slip while cleansing, which is especially helpful for dry, textured or highly manipulated hair,” she says. “If I'm shampooing dry or textured hair and it immediately feels tangled and rough, I know I'm creating more work for myself later. This has a richer, more luxurious lather than people sometimes expect from a hydrating shampoo, and it leaves hair feeling clean without that squeaky, stripped feeling.”

Leave it to tennis star Sloane Stephens to create one of our team’s favorite shampoos. After a sweaty Rumble boxing class, Doc&Glo helped bring that fresh salon feeling to features director Rachel Epstein's shower. The first thing she noticed was the gel-like consistency of the shampoo, which easily lathers in her hands—she only needs two to three pumps. But her favorite part was the calming peppermint-and-eucalyptus scent that lingered for the rest of the night. “None of that fruity garbage over here,” she says.

Epstein has used the shampoo and conditioner twice a week for the last month, and her scalp has consistently felt balanced. Her waves are fresher and fuller the next day. “Because I have dandruff, I still need to use a medicated shampoo here and there, but I’ll definitely continue using this duo,” she says.

Chlorine and hard water can fade your color-treated hair and make neutral and cool tones look warm. This de-brassing shampoo reduces yellowing and brassiness in blonde, highlighted, silver, and gray hair. “I have seen great results with this, and there's no purple buildup,” says Kennor, who especially likes this one for double-process blondes.

Foster appreciates that Virtue isn’t relying solely on heavy purple dye. The tone is actually synthetic color-free and dye-free. De-Brassing Shampoo pairs botanical ingredients with Virtue’s signature Alpha Keratin 60ku protein, a proprietary protein that mimics the hair-strengthening, damage-repairing benefits of keratin.

When you want a splurge-worthy shampoo, opt for this recent Women’s Health Beauty Award winner. “If you color your hair, you need a shampoo that protects your investment,” says beauty director Brian Underwood. “With a sulfate-free formula that ensures your scalp won’t become irritated, this one contains ingredients that soothe, repair, and rejuvenate like grapeseed sterols, chia seed, and hook seaweed.” It also contains a trifecta of quinoa extract, chamomile extract, and amaranth extract to soften, smooth, hydrate, and condition hair.

A bonus: It gently foams up while strengthening and hydrating your highlighted, bleached, or color-treated hair, adds Foster.

K18 is beloved by everyone from Foster and me to the legendary Simone Biles. Peptide Prep is pH-optimized and contains the brand’s signature K18 Peptide along with plant-derived surfactants. “It cleanses without adding stress to already compromised hair,” says Foster. “That's important because damaged hair doesn't need to be babied to the point that it's not being properly cleansed, but it also doesn't need an aggressive shampoo every wash day.” It’s also made with salicylic acid, which gently exfoliates and removes excess scalp oil.

After using this shampoo, I experienced less flaking and less product buildup from heat protectants and scalp oils. My hair feels lighter and bouncier, and I can get away with shampooing once a week instead of twice a week since using this product.

Redken's Acidic Bonding Concentrate is another product Foster likes for chemically processed or damaged hair. “Citric acid is a key component of the formula, designed to help reinforce weakened bonds while maintaining an acidic pH,” she says.

I tried this one during its launch in February and continued using it for several months afterward. My scalp felt so incredibly clean, without that pesky tightness and dryness. When paired with the matching conditioner, I noticed less shedding in my shower. My strands felt more resilient, conditioned, and rebalanced. I also noticed that my hair’s balayage took longer to fade, which is a major win.

Caring for fine hair is tricky because it may need moisture and strengthening but can become flat very quickly if the formula is too rich, says Foster. Ouai contains hydrolyzed keratin, biotin, and chia seed oil to leave your fine hair bouncy without that heavy, overly-conditioned feeling.

This shampoo also suds up in a rich, satisfying way, adding a luxurious touch to the mornings of deputy editor Carina Hsieh. “My hair has more lift at the roots—almost the way it used to, pre-30s,” she says. “My bangs are banging again (physically, emotionally, and, of course, spiritually), and my hair no longer separates into the same three sad little strands it seemed to automatically separate every 2 PM.”

To Hsieh, it only faintly smells of rose and musk. It’s the same fragrance as Ouai’s pet shampoo, but she swears the pet shampoo smells better. “But honestly, that’s me really looking for a negative as I sit and twirl my hair all day,” she says.

“Design Essentials is my absolute favorite shampoo,” says Foster. “The brand has been working with textured hair long before it became a trending topic, and that experience shows with Honey Crème.” This shampoo cleanses while providing slip and helping with detangling. As its name implies, it’s enriched with honey, a moisture-preserving, quick-lathering ingredient that helps soften and smooth the cuticle, says Foster.

You can also use this shampoo if you don’t have curly or coily strands, though you might not need the extra help with detangling. Still, it’s an enjoyable experience at a fantastic price point. “The best shampoo isn’t necessarily the most expensive one. It's the one that cleanses your scalp effectively while respecting what your hair needs at that particular time,” says Foster, and Design Essentials proves that with Honey Crème.

I’ve been using Design Essentials since I was in high school. It’s a truly reliable brand that hasn’t compromised on ingredient quality, smell, or feel. My hair is truly softer and more manageable every single time I use this shampoo.

Joico’s Detox Shampoo does just that—it combines a proprietary chelating agent and activated charcoal to remove product buildup and hard-water deposits. This color-safe shampoo also removes trace minerals and salts.

While it’s tough on unwanted components that can compromise my hair's integrity, it also contains moringa seed oil to help prevent dryness. There are also veggie proteins intended to help strengthen weak hair bonds, leaving me with a noticeably cleaner scalp and healthy-looking hair.

Whenever I use this shampoo, my hair feels super clean, but still hydrated. With each wash, my hair is noticeably bouncier, giving me a fresh-from-the-salon look. I also appreciate that this shampoo is compatible with all hair types. My hair is thick and coily, while my mom has fine, color-treated straight hair. This formula worked for both of us, and it has recently become a must-have for her since moving to a new city with hard water.

#4823. The 13 Best T-Shirts for Men, According to Style Experts

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Mack Weldon and Gildan came out on top in our testing.

IF YOU’RE BUILDING a better wardrobe, start with your T-shirts. Pick the right one, and it can make your shoulders look broader, show off your chest, and make your whole outfit sharper. Pick the wrong one, and suddenly even clean jeans can’t save you. That’s why the bar for a good T-shirt should be higher than most guys set it—you want one that works under a hoodie, looks great solo with denim, or even under a blazer if you’re feeling bold.

More mensweat brands are treating them seriously too, with upgraded fabrics, sharper cuts, and construction built to go the distance. The key is knowing where to invest. If you need something to throw on around the house, an affordable multipack makes sense, but make sure it holds up to swear and repeated washes. But if the tee is going to carry an outfit—or at the gym—it’s worth spending a little extra for something that fits right and will last. We’ve tested tees from every menswear brand on the market to find the best ones for work, workouts, and everywhere in between.

At Men's Health, our fashion editors have worn, washed, and wowed in more T-shirts than you can count. That said, when we vouch for one, believe us. My ultimate favorite is this crew neck version from Mack Weldon, which is made with Supima cotton, aka the softest, strongest, and most durable cotton. It feels like a second skin, breathes well, and the slim fit is flattering. I’m 5'8" and wear a size small, and it hugs my biceps and pecs with just the right amount of tightness while still leaving plenty of breathing room.

I’ve worn this tee during errands, and I found that it's managed to retain its soft touch and original shape after multiple washes. The infused stretch makes this a cinch to move in, whether I was reaching for something in a high cabinet or putting my luggage in the plane's overhead compartment. Plus, every seam is super reinforced so it can handle tons of mileage without a single thread giving in.

I’m not kidding when I say I’ve worn this just about everywhere. Since it's woven with antimicrobial silver threads that fight odor-causing bacteria, I've used it as a workout shirt for serious sweat sessions and stayed smelling fresh. Performance aside, I’ve made this tee work in a bunch of settings: rocking it with jeans for an everyday look, and even layering it under a blazer when I want to dress things up. Plus, it's available in a variety of colors to choose from.

Read More: Mack Weldon Silver Crew Neck T-Shirt Review

Need to stock up on T-shirts? Gildan has you covered with this bestselling multipack, which our editors rave about for its breathable cotton fabric, moisture-wicking finish, and an easy to move in fit. Even though this tee isn’t blended with any spandex or elastane, I was surprised by how easily I could lift my arms and not feel any stiffness or tugging. It didn’t feel like I was wearing a cardboard box. I especially appreciate the classic crew neckline that sits around the neck and doesn’t stretch out after a few wears like most budget packs tend to do.

I typically don’t wear this as a workout tee, but it makes for an excellent undershirt beneath my zip-up hoodies and sweaters. And when I layered it, the tee conforms to my body and stays put. Unlike stretchy shirts that can ride up or bunch, this one stays flat. It’s so soft, thin (but not see-through), and holds shape remarkably well, even after multiple wash cycles.

Now let’s talk shrinkage: I ran it through a normal cold wash and tumble dried on a low heat. It did shrink a bit: about a half inch in length and slightly in the sleeves. But honestly, that ended up making the fit better for me. It hugged around my pecs, molded closer to the torso, and the sleeves hit a more flattering midpoint on my upper arm to show my muscle gains. Plus, it doesn’t pill as quickly as one would imagine, based on the price.

Read more: Gildan Crew Neck T-Shirt Review

Vuori, one of our favorite athleisure brands, uses moisture-wicking tech fabric in its signature crewneck tee, providing unparalleled comfort while you're running a 5K or just running errands. Unlike with other standard athletic shirts that always fit too tight, I didn't have to go through that trouble myself with this slim fit take, making it a tee I'd actually wear out on its own, because outside is where it shines: To me, its stretch and moisture-wicking have made it look and smell fresh time after time. More importantly, I couldn’t believe how soft it felt when I put it on the first time. It was like being clothed in a cloud, and the breathable fabric was able to keep me cool instead of suffocating me.

Anyone who’s owned merino wool knows the entry price is worth the investment. The fabric is famously breathable, and its natural anti-odor properties and moisture-wicking ability make it so you can wear the garment for longer than you'd expect before it gets, well, gross. To test out its merino wool performance, I’ve in fact packed this tee for a recent trip and worn it to hike, walk, and commute for a few days. At the end of the day, when I did take it off, I was delighted to find out that it remained as fresh as when I first put it on, after all those hours of traveling in it.

Winner of our Fitness Awards’ best short sleeve tee, Rhone’s Reign is perhaps the most comfortable workout T-shirt the athletic guys at Men's Health have ever tested and worn to a gym session. "This breathable top moves with you when you reach overhead for pull-ups and chin-ups thanks to its seamless construction," says our fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S..

In addition, its breathable, moisture-wicking fabric has always come in a pinch for me whenever the gym gets a bit too heated. No matter how intense our sessions can be, I still feel and smell fresh after sweating bullets, thanks to the anti-odor technology.

A couple of years ago, the Los Angeles-based Buck Mason purchased two century-old knitting mills in Eastern Pennsylvania that were on the verge of closure. Now all of the brand’s T-shirts are produced there, from the raw cotton to the finished products. Vertically integrated production like that provides a level of quality control that is evident in the Slub Classic Tee. There were no loose threads or out-of-place stitching, the cut was perfectly balanced, and tremendously sturdy for a relatively lightweight tee.

Our editors love this t-shirt because the weight hits a sweet spot that is surprisingly hard to find. For a while now, most t-shirts have been a little flimsy. Heavyweight cotton tees have made a big comeback recently, but many of these are just a little too bulky. Buck Mason’s slub cotton has a soft feel and loose drape while still feeling sturdy and reliable. The white tee is slightly transparent, but with a speckled texture indicative of slub cotton. It is truly a do-it-all t-shirt that looks good with everything and fits well on most body types.

Sunspel is one of those English brands that just gets premium basics. It's been perfecting the art of simple, high-quality clothing since 1860, and its Riviera Midweight T-shirt is proof the makers know exactly what they're doing. Originally created for James Bond (yep, Daniel Craig wore it in Casino Royale), this tee is elevated but effortless, crafted from Supima cotton.

We're big fans of this material because it's extra-long staple, meaning its fibers are naturally longer than regular cotton, increasing its durability and, ultimately, its lifespan. It's buttery soft yet structured with a tailored-but-not-too-tight fit, making it one of the tees you can dress up or down without a second thought.

During our testing, we found it doesn't pill or wrinkle easily. The slightly shorter length looks better untucked and drapes neatly over your jeans. Plus, it arrives in a whopping 22 colors, so you have every hue to choose from.

Reigning Champ is one of the few clothing brands out there that mills its own fabrics. While the fabric is called mid-weight, it felt sturdier to us than most tees we tried out. The boxy fit was extremely comfortable, with ’90s-inspired sleeves that are on the longer and wider side. This is especially beneficial for guys with broader shoulders and bigger biceps.

The flatlock seam construction along the sleeves, shoulders, and sides is more commonly seen in sweatshirts, with this being the only T-shirt on the list to feature it. It was a nice touch because flatlock seams reduce friction points, which is especially helpful with a heavier fabric like this one. We noticed the benefit after wearing this tee all day, especially along the shoulder.

Cos offers a ribbed T-shirt that looks and feels much more elevated than your average basic tee. It’s crafted from an organic and recycled cotton-blend jersey that has plenty of stretch and flex, but still substantial in hand. The 230gsm (grams per square meter) fabric gives it a weighty, premium feel without making it stiff or heavy to wear all day. Like the Uniqlo tee, this neckline has a reinforced binding that keeps the neckline from drooping over time. The ribbed texture also adds visual interest, so it feels more styled up than a standard flat cotton top.

I toss this tee in the wash and let it air dry to help preserve the shape and texture.

Some necklines on T-shirts tend to droop or stretch after a few wears or washes, but the binding at Uniqlo’s collar helps this one keep its shape. The neckline design is inspired by military vintage tees, which gives it a rugged edge while still looking polished enough to wear on its own. That durability stems from its heavyweight cotton jersey fabric, which feels structured without being overly stiff. It’s thick enough to keep me warm when layered under an open flannel or leather jacket in cooler weather, though I probably might opt for something lighter in high 80s temperatures. Unlike thinner tees, this one has a clean drape that looks good untucked or tucked in trousers or jeans. The fit is not too boxy or too slim, so it works pretty much on every body type with sizes up to 3XL. You grab it in a bunch of easy neutrals for the office, but there are also pops of color like orange or green—the latter being my go-to in the summer.

Simply put, this is a quintessential pocket tee available for a very affordable price. It feels like it was pulled from Gap’s ’90s archive, when the brand was known for great-looking basics. The fit was a little boxy, but by no means baggy, and looked flattering on a whole range of body types. Even though the construction details are simple, especially compared to some of the premium tees we tested, it still felt sturdy and reliable.

The weight of this tee came as a surprise, given the look and price. It felt more like a midweight cotton that held its shape better than most "basic" T-shirts we’ve tried in the past.

Everlane has a talent for making high-quality, affordable basics that can fit seamlessly into pretty much any wardrobe. The Essential Organic Crew is a perfect example of the brand’s mastery of fit, fabric, and colors that have mass appeal while still looking cool. Boxy shoulders, wider sleeves, and a collar that sat just right provided a relaxed feel in our testing, which was perfect for lounging around and casual everyday wear. We wanted to highlight the fabric, not only because it's a sturdy pure cotton jersey, but it comes with a unique washed finish. Each fit brings its own flavor to the table, so whether you’re going for a sleek, body-conscious look or maximum comfort on a lazy day, there’s a T-shirt out there that’s up your alley. Here, we break down the most common cuts to consider.

This tee is tailored to follow your body’s lines without feeling snug. Go for this if you want your tee to show off your hard-earned gains.

Classic fit tees offer a balanced cut that isn’t too tight or too loose. They drape nicely over any frame, delivering a no-fuss, everyday look that looks great under a blazer, bomber jacket, or on its own on casual Fridays. It’s a reliable go-to when you want to keep your fit simple yet sharp.

When comfort is your mantra, a relaxed fit is where it’s at. These tees give you plenty of room to breathe and move.

Built for the guy with a muscular build, athletic fit tees have broader shoulders and a narrower waist. They’re engineered to give your jacked upper body the space it needs without turning you into a walking grocery bag.

100% cotton tees are often the gold standard for everyday tees, but cotton often doesn’t perform the best, which is why tech-blended fabrics can give useful features like moisture-wicking, four-way stretch, and breathability. Hence, if you're an active guy, or maybe you sweat a lot naturally, or are looking for tees for going out, ditch the full cotton and opt for blended fabrics. Below is an overview of the kinds of materials to choose from.

The classic choice. Think: breathable, soft, and natural cotton. Whether it's combed, ring-spun, or Pima, pure cotton tees just get better with each wash.

All the comfort of regular cotton, but grown without harsh chemicals. It's eco-friendly and feels extra gentle on your skin.

When cotton teams up with polyester or rayon, you get a tee that's more durable, resists shrinkage, and sometimes even wrinkles less. It's all about that low-maintenance vibe.

These are designed for action. Performance blends often feature polyester or moisture-wicking fibers to keep you cool and dry. Whether you're hitting the gym or commuting, these tees move with you and manage sweat like a champ.

Different styles of tees work best for different occasions. For instance, a V-neck T-shirt works best as an undershirt and can make your neck look longer. And if you want to look dressy in T-shirts, ditch the plain-looking ones that look like undershirts and go for a pocketed tee instead. Better yet, opt for graphic tees to really make a style statement that is true to you.

To find the best t-shirts for men, our style team led by Style and Reviews Director, Christian Gollayan has personally tried on over 60 different options since 2020 and tested each of them for at least two weeks by wearing them in all sorts of situations. We vetted our tested options by making notes of their style, type, comfort, fit, price point, durability, versatility, and performance such as stretch, moisture-wicking, and breathability.

We examined whether they fit well and true to size, whether their fabric could withstand hours of movement in different temperatures, how the collar stood up after multiple wears, and whether they could be worn for more than one occasion. We also tested these T-shirts on different body types, from slim to athletic to buff, to ensure the most unbiased results.

Specifically, we're looking for T-shirt styles that are not trendy or trend-chasing (so no funky graphics, baggy fits, or holes here); instead, our picks for the best t-shirts for men all fit great even on buff guys, provide a ton of value at reasonable price points, and come in styles that will look great years from now. Opt for lightweight, breathable T-shirts. Style them with shorts or casual linen pants for a cool and relaxed look. Slip into comfortable sandals or boat shoes for added comfort.

Pair a relaxed-fit or classic-fit tee with casual joggers or sweatpants for a totally easy vibe.

Style a light and breezy T-shirt with swim trunks or linen shorts for a beach-ready look. Wear flip-flops or sandals to complement the vacation vibe.

Pick moisture-wicking or performance T-shirts first, and wear them with gym shorts or athletic shorts or track pants for maximum comfort and flexibility during your activities.

If you know the dress code allows, pick a well-fitted (usually slim) T-shirt in a solid color and minimal design (no pocket, for instance). Pair it with tailored trousers or chinos for a more polished appearance (make sure to tuck it), then layer it under a blazer. Complete the look with dress sneakers or leather sneakers.

The most popular and reputable T-shirt brands for men that consistently deliver high-quality tees often happen to be the best clothing brands for men. For instance, Calvin Klein, J.Crew, and Sunspel often churn out classic tees in premium materials suitable for both casual and smart-casual occasions. Buck Mason and Billy Reid are known for making casual pocketed tees with a lived-in vibe and garment-dyed fabric.

Athleisure brands like Vuori, Lululemon, and Rhone make t-shirts that are versatile for all kinds of physical activities. Trendy brands like CDLP, Everlane, and Richer Poorer are what you should go to for relaxed-fit, oversized tees. For undershirts or tees for homebodies, Tommy John, Jockey, Calvin Klein, and Hanes have you covered.

Our all-time favorite, tried-and-tested t-shirt brand, however, is Mack Weldon, which makes tees that are soft, versatile, long-lasting, well-fitted, and can do no wrong.

That depends on the occasion and personal style. For a casual look, you can't go wrong with a classic crew neck T-shirt (especially those that have gone through the wash to look more vintage and lived-in). V-necks add a touch of flair and work great as undershirts. Graphic tees let you showcase your personality, while T-shirts with a pocket let you look a bit more sophisticated. For athletic activities, moisture-wicking and performance t-shirts are a no-brainer when you go to the gym or hike.

Providing the right care to your tees will help keep them looking sharp and feeling comfy for eons. First up, read the damn label! Make sure you follow the washing instructions. Also, be sure to separate colors when you wash T-shirts (i.e. darks with darks and lights with lights).

When you wash, make sure the water is cold because the temperature will help preserve colors and prevent shrinkage. Turning T-shirts inside out can also help protect the outer fabric from friction and fading. Use a gentle cycle and mild detergent to help maintain the shape and fabric, too.

Additionally, skip the dryer and air-dry if possible because high heat can cause shrinkage (use low-heat settings if you must air-dry). We also recommend folding instead of hanging T-shirts because the latter will stretch out the neck of the tees and cause them to lose their shape.

These are two indicators of whether your T-shirt can or should be tucked in or left untucked. With a curved hem, then the tee is best left untucked; it'll probably look better that way. A straight hem can do both, depending on the length. That is to say, a longer length is thus best left tucked in, unless you've got the height or the style magic to offset any disproportion.

#4822. South Korea’s crypto bill could move stablecoin race beyond token issuance

South Korea’s draft bill favors bank-led stablecoin issuance but allows fintech and technology companies to become the largest individual shareholders.

South Korean fintech companies could gain influence in bank-led stablecoin groups by signing up partners that help people spend won-denominated tokens, Tiger Research said in its Tuesday report.

“Those relationships are likely to matter more to the business than the volume of stablecoins issued,” the Asia-focused research company said.

On Tuesday, South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) unveiled its draft digital assets bill that would initially limit issuance of won-denominated stablecoins to consortiums in which banks collectively hold a majority stake. A fintech or technology company could still hold a larger stake than any individual bank.

The proposal follows months of regulatory disagreements. The Bank of Korea has advocated for bank-led issuance, citing monetary policy and financial stability risks, while the FSC previously favored allowing nonbank companies to issue stablecoins.

If the Banking Act’s 15% limit on a bank’s stake in a nonfinancial company applies to stablecoin issuers, at least four banks would need to join each consortium to secure a majority, according to Tiger Research.

Vincent Chok, founder and CEO of First Digital, whose subsidiary issues the FDUSD stablecoin, told Cointelegraph that bank-majority consortiums could give won-denominated stablecoins credibility at launch, while fintech participation could help preserve innovation.

“Beyond who issues, Korea’s ability to capture the wider economic activity around stablecoins will rest on efficient on- and off-ramps and rails connecting KRW with global dollar liquidity,” Chok said.

South Korean financial and technology companies have already started exploring these opportunities. In May, KB Financial Group completed a won-denominated stablecoin pilot covering merchant payments and cross-border remittances. In July, Viva Republica, which operates the Toss payments app, partnered with Optimism and Sunnyside Labs to test stablecoin-based payments for financial institutions.

Related: How South Korea’s proposed 20% cap could change who runs Upbit

The bill still needs to pass the National Assembly before proceeding to presidential promulgation. Tiger Research said the legislation is expected to take effect one year after promulgation, while key details, including shareholder requirements for stablecoin consortiums, remain subject to subsequent enforcement decrees.

#4821. Mauviel's Copper Cookware Is 25% Off For Black Friday

There are a few covetable luxury goods you’ll see pop up again and again in AD’s home tours: a Moccamaster coffee maker, a Nordic Knots rug, and Mauviel copper cookware, to name a few. As seen in this Sag Harbor home, this Parisian pied-à-terre, this Westchester residence, and this Connecticut country retreat, Mauviel is something of a status symbol in kitchens. Much like a Le Creuset Dutch oven out on display, spying a few copper pans from the French brand hanging from a rail signals that “Great Taste Lives Here.” And this week marks a good opportunity to join the club, with Mauviel sets and individual pieces up to 30% off for Black Friday at Williams Sonoma and on Shop.

I’m a recent convert; I bought my Mauviel frying pan mostly to elevate the aesthetic of my kitchen, with a suspicion that the tool would also function as a fantastic piece of cookware, particularly for my beloved morning ritual of frying up an egg for breakfast. Of course it does. Unlike some of my ceramic pans that catch and dry out an egg, the Mauviel has given me no trouble, delivering me the most perfect eggs to date I’ve ever cooked. Even against my stainless-steel pans (which I do love very much), these heat a bit more quickly and evenly.

That excellent cooking capability is largely due to the construction and craftsmanship of the goods, which have a long history as a French culinary staple. Mauviel has made copper cookware since 1830 in Villedieu-les-Poêles, a town in Normandy with an enduring history of copper manufacturing; the pieces are still handcrafted there. As far as their makeup, the M’150 B pieces are, for example, 1.5 millimeters thick and constructed of a 90% polished copper exterior and a 10% stainless-steel interior. They heat evenly; are immediately responsive to heat adjustments; and work on gas, electric, and ceramic cooktops.

The pans partners with a copper kettle on the stove in this Portland manse by Jessica Helgerson.

The copper treasures do, however, require care. They’re not nonstick pots and pans, so you need a little oil or butter to get any slip. They’re hand-wash only, and Mauviel advises against using them for long stretches on high heat or leaving them empty on a hot burner. I don’t polish mine, simply because I don’t own any copper polish. The wear shows quickly, and I like that, though if AD were shooting my house, maybe I’d like it less.

The Black Friday markdowns run across the line: my copper fry pan is going for $280 in the 10-inch size (25% off), a 2.5-quart sauce pan is $450 (29% off), and a 15-piece cookware set is $3,000 (32% off). For anyone who cooks every day, it’s a hard gift to beat. I, for one, now can’t imagine frying my eggs any other way.

#4820. Latest Canadian budget packs funding for 55,000 new EV chargers

Canada’s government wants to make it easier for citizens to drive electric, and they’re putting more than $4 billion in funding for electricity infrastructure and grid modernization that includes more than 55,000 new EV chargers.

The proposed federal budget set aside $4 billion (CAD) for grid improvements, with a $~635 million carveout specifically for EV charging infrastructure with $587 million of that set aside to renew the Zero-Emission Vehicle Infrastructure Program (ZEVIP), which funds the development of new public EV charging stations.

“The charging industry is really encouraged by the multi-year investment in the budget,” explains Travis Allan, president and CEO of the Canadian Charging Infrastructure Council (CCIC) told Electric Autonomy. “We’ll be looking to make sure that we have great programs in place to deal with the barriers faced by people living in condos and apartments, public fast charging, which needs to cover major corridors and metropolitan areas, and then also charging for fleets and medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, which make up a major share of transportation emissions.”

The rest of the $4 billion will be spent on electricity infrastructure expansion over the next 10 years, starting in 2027 and running through 2036. Because it’s Canada where nearly 60% of electrical generation already comes from renewable hydro and wind power, renewable energy is a de-facto priority, with carveouts for the Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program, new data and modeling efforts to guide grid planning, and $1.6 billion to modernize power systems in northern and remote communities.

The charging infrastructure program highlighted here, ZEVIP, would help charge point operators by covering up to 50% of eligible project expenses for most projects, and up to 75% of projects led by indigenous developers with caps of up to $2 million per project.

Canada continues to take steps to separate itself from the wild swings and economic chaos caused by America’s random tariffs, trade policies, and dumb oil wars – and building out an infrastructure that makes it easier for its citizens to give affordable Chinese EVs a chance while strengthening its relationship with the US’ biggest economic rival?

The couple reveal their hidden skills during a round of “In Fitness and In Health.”

Husband-and-wife duo Nelly and Ashanti aren’t just hip-hop royalty—they’re reality TV stars too. #4818. 15 Best Places to Buy Bedding, Editor Picks (2026)

Sheets get slept in every night and washed every week (in theory) which means it doesn’t take long to learn which ones hold up under use. Every retailer here comes recommended by an AD editor or contributor who has lived with the bedding at home for a long stretch: flannel kept on the bed through May, linen hauled to a communal laundromat and back, or a sheet set that survives a dog digging in every night.

Each brand earned its spot for a reason, whether that’s price, a cooling fabric, an unusually wide color range, or embroidery done by hand. Rest assured: they’re all comfy.

For bedding basics that won’t damage the budget, Quince is our first stop. Its European Linen Sheet Set earned our pick for the best affordable linen sheets, and senior shopping editor Nashia Baker has recently added the brand to her list of favorites. “The price point is unbeatable, and I love that they offer bedding sets in beautiful colorways and a variety of fabric options,” she says. “The quality is also impressive, especially considering the affordability.”

Made from 100% European flax, the sheets cost a fraction of what competitors charge, thanks in part to Quince’s direct-to-consumer model which skips traditional retail markups. “I love its airy nature along with the gorgeous Bordeaux color that complements the rest of my decor,” says Baker. The bedding range extends to quilts and coverlets, , and the brand’s down comforter also made our ranking of the best comforters.

Anyone who has paused a Nancy Meyers movie to study the bedroom should start with Serena & Lily. The brand is based in Sausalito, California, but its textured, breezy bedding and decor would look right at home on any coast, Nantucket included. The range covers lightweight linen and crisp cotton percale in pale colors and easygoing prints.

Of all the bedding Baker has tested, the Nantucket Stripe Sheet Set ranks near the top for its light weight and “worn-in texture,” which keeps the linen soft instead of scratchy. The ruffle trim keeps her bed from looking too plain. “The striped mink print does give a seaside vibe, but it’s been neutral enough to layer with any color bed cover without clashing with the rest of my minimal, romantic decor over the few months I’ve tested the set,” she adds. For a top layer, there’s the scalloped Baywood Quilt, which Alpert likes as a light blanket for “when you want to throw something over while you read your favorite Emily Henry book in bed.”

Boll & Branch sheets arrive feeling as if they’ve already been through several wash cycles, without the fraying or pilling that usually comes with that. Contributor Rachel Fletcher tested the brand’s percale, Supima cotton, flannel, and linen, but its signature sateen stood out most for its long-staple cotton and a soft, smooth finish. “That extra-soft feel, paired with the lovely, cooling properties, make them feel like the luxury sheets they are,” she says. Converts can outfit the rest of the room too, with Boll & Branch’s mattresses and bedroom furniture.

Brooklinen started out selling two things, cotton percale and sateen sheets, and has since added cashmere, brushed flannel, and a long list of prints. Pieces come in bundled sets or one at a time, and prices land between the budget brands and the luxury labels. Our editors keep coming back to the linen sheets, which they use in every season.

“Since I don’t live my life on a Greek island, I thought white linen sheets year-round might be a slightly bold move, but the nature of the fiber is versatile and temperature regulating,” says AD contributor Madeleine Luckel, who tested the Core Sheet Set. Fletcher sleeps on the Luxe Sheet Set and credits it with keeping her cool. “I’m a hot sleeper with sensitive skin, and they’re really cool on my skin at night, which is a huge relief,” she says. “I love the breathability of these sheets.”

Few bedding brands have tied their name to sustainability as closely as Coyuchi. Its linen sheets are made from certified organic French flax grown without synthetic fertilizers or pesticides, and the brand also offers percale, sateen, and flannel sheets. The earthy color palette is a selling point on its own.

“I love the color, which is what drew me to these sheets in the first place,” says Sam Cochran, global features editor. “They’re the perfect brown—a tad auburn, ever so slightly timeworn in palette.”

Shopping writer Julia Harrison and contributor Kate McGregor agree: Garnet Hill is their “secret spot” for bedding. Harrison is devoted to the flannel sheets and admits she leaves them on the bed through May because “they’re so soft, I’d rather suffer in my own sweat than switch them out.” The ticking stripe is “perfectly classic—like a true vintage piece, but not actually vintage…that might be tough sell in the bedding department.” Alpert also loves her flannel pick, a duvet cover that “signals a cottagecore moment without going over the top.” Paired with her Ostermoor duvet insert, it’s “like climbing under a layer of meringue.” Garnet Hill specializes in vintage-inspired designs, patchwork quilts especially, made in 100% linen and 100% cotton options at reasonable prices.

Cozy Earth makes breathable bedding for people who run hot at night, and its signature bamboo bedding, made of 100% viscose, are the brand’s best-known example. “I honestly thought these sheets were silk,” says contributor Megan Wahn. “That’s how smooth and soft they feel.” Wahn tested them mostly in winter, and despite feeling cool to the touch, they kept her warm. “I’m especially eager to see how they perform in the summer,” she adds. “Something about their smoothness makes me think the summer-night sweats won’t stand a chance.”

Parachute is where we send anyone after classic, well-made cotton bedding. Its sets and bundles are designed with sustainability in mind, and the percale and brushed cotton are made by artisans at the brand’s factory in Portugal.

“We love [Parachute] because the bedding is designed to provide a hotel-like experience, offering a perfect balance of softness and crispness,” says Stephanie Kraus of Stephanie Kraus Designs, whose clients favor the brand’s linen bedding sets. “They become softer with each wash while maintaining their durability and are super soft to sleep in every night.”

Fletcher also praises the brand’s commitment to organic, ethically sourced materials; the Organic Cloud Cotton Duvet Set, for one, is made of Oeko-Tex-certified 100% cotton. “I try a lot of bedding in this line of work and the more I do, the more I appreciate ethical and organic production, even if the price tag is a little higher,” she says.

GreenRow makes charming, long-lasting bedding from recycled and sustainably sourced materials, and it has won over several people on the Shop AD team. Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert calls the Helena Floral Sheet Set “without a doubt, the softest sheets I own.” She compares the cotton satin to velvet, and the butter-yellow florals and green micro-gingham ruffle make the set prettier still. McGregor, meanwhile, is partial to the reversible patchwork quilt. “It’s the kind of blanket that feels substantial without trapping heat or feeling stuffy,” she notes. “I feel cocooned without a down comforter, but I’m not smothered when I sleep sans AC in the warmer months. It’s a year-round bedding piece for me, especially since the color palette can lean moodier or more cheerful depending on my sheet selection.”

Rebecca Udall is a newer name and one worth knowing. Her namesake bedding line is built on romantic, careful details, such as soft-colored decorative embroidery along the sheets. McGregor’s current favorite is this scalloped percale sheet set. “The feel is like a washed percale, crisp but forgiving, and I find that the subtle color on the detailed edge gives the perfect amount of visual interest to my all-white bedscape,” she says. If you want less ornament, try the Georgiana duvet cover, with faint ladderstitch detailing hand-embroidered by artisans in Northern Italy.

Hommey, an Australian brand founded in 2020, first caught on with its boldly striped robes and nightwear. It has since carried those designs into cotton and linen sheets and duvet covers. Across both fabrics, there are more than two dozen colors and prints to choose from. For maximalists who want to try color-blocking, the brand’s bolder colorways are a great place to start.

Baker tested the brown sugar linen duvet cover and found the stonewashed, Oeko-Tex certified flax smoother and more broken-in straight out of the package than the Quince version she already owned (above). “I won’t get ahead of myself and say it feels like pure silk, but I can confirm that it’s soft and breathable almost like an organic cotton duvet after a few washes,” Baker says. She pairs the chocolatey shade with burgundy linen sheets for a moodier bed, though it also works as a neutral with lighter sheets in oatmeal, which pick up the cream trim. The one drawback is that the cover has no interior ties, so the insert can shift around inside.

Australian brand Cultiver makes linen sheets and duvets with an easy, beachy look. Its Oeko-Tex certified pieces are an investment, and a worthwhile one. Coverlets are generously sized so they drape loosely, and the envelope-back pillow cases hold their shape without looking stiff. Fletcher has put her set through heavy use and many wash cycles. “Linen is my bedding fabric of choice pretty much 365 days a year, and Cultiver’s high-quality sheet sets do it for me in a way no other brand has. Out of all the sets I’ve tried, this one has stood the test of many washes, my dog digging in them to get cozy at night, and surviving across seasons without feeling worn or threadbare,” she says.

Erica Tanov’s bedding is handmade by artisans in Jaipur, in 100% linen with embroidery drawn from traditional Indian textiles. Harrison calls hers “a lifetime set” that “draws more compliments than anything else in my apartment.” The linen is soft and tough: She hauls this sheet set to her neighborhood laundromat, and it survives the communal machines without damage. It’s the first linen set she’s found to be “city-friendly,” as she calls it. She hasn’t tried the quilts or throw blankets yet, though one already tops her birthday wishlist (this one).

It depends mostly on how you like your bed to feel and how reliable your thermostat is. If you like the crisp coolness of hotel sheets, try percale. If you like a soft, organic feel, try linen for a breezy texture, or bamboo sheets for something similar to silk. Cotton sheets (like Supima sets) are often the most durable over time, especially after many, many washes. Your warmest options are generally flannel sets, and your coolest are generally bamboo and percale. For a basic setup, we recommend a full sheet set (flat sheet included, people) plus a duvet insert with a cover. The cover protects the insert and keeps it clean, so you’ll generally only need to wash the insert every six months rather than weekly like your sheets. Harrison likes to go one step further with a bed blanket underneath her duvet and above her sheets for a bit of weight and additional warmth. If a fluffy duvet isn’t your thing, a quilt or coverlet can take its place and add a little more weight.

Start with the fiber content on the label. Search for 100% cotton, linen (the more organic, the better), and steer clear of polyesters or more plastic fibers, as they’re likely to pill more quickly and break apart in the washer and dryer.
