#4755. Where to Buy Photography Prints Online, Vetted by AD (2026)

Photos have the power to add personality to your home’s art collection, showcasing a distinct mood or point of view while boosting your space’s aesthetic. Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz’s San Diego home is a masterclass in this craft. Among the antique African woodwork and abstract ceramics sit carefully placed Gordon Parks photographs that layer in a new, thought-provoking dimension to the artwork in their home.

This ability to infuse varied mediums in your house isn’t reserved for just the Grammy-winning artists of the world; as long as you know where to look, weaving photography into your home is quite an attainable undertaking. Below, we’ve rounded up our favorite places to buy prints online. Whether you’re searching for a one-of-one vintage photograph, a tool to help you exhibit your own snaps, or a photo collection that removes the guesswork from the curation process, these sites can help you add a personal touch to your interiors.

Want to display high-quality artistic photographs without breaking the bank? Desenio can help. The site offers contemporary and abstract art prints that can add visual interest to modern interiors, and many of the pieces cost far less than $100. Add natural sophistication with a dramatic leaf print or evoke a sense of intimacy with a close-up portrait of the human form. With multiple sizes and frames available, you can snag a couple of smaller photos to complete your gallery wall, or make a statement with one large print to hang over a bed or sofa.

It’s a shame for those candid moments among friends and stunning vacation sunsets to stay trapped and largely unseen in your phone’s camera roll. That’s where Framebridge comes in, printing your images onto high-quality photo paper and encasing them in custom frames. The company also offers photo layouts with life-size hanging guides to help you wall-mount your images with the accuracy and precision that they deserve. Essentially, Framebridge streamlines the entire framing process to be easy and accessible, elevating family photos and artistic stills alike.

If you’re a fine art aficionado who is hoping to track down rare finds, 1stDibs is the platform for you. While it also sells vintage and designer furniture, the fine art photography collection is unmatched. You can purchase pieces from legendary fashion photographers, like this signed portrait of Whoopi Goldberg by Annie Leibovitz, as well as avant-garde photographs like “Africaine, No. 2,” by Shawn Theodore. With photographs and photo books spanning styles and price points, it’s easy to get lost in a sea of beautiful images. Use the brand’s curated pages to narrow your search to specific focuses, like color photography or figurative photography.

If you’re a homesick West Coaster or an East Coaster with California dreams, your next piece should come from Lndn Gray. Peruse the site for landscape photography that embodies the surrealist loneliness of the Pacific shores or for a still life that romanticizes the raucous rock-star culture of Los Angeles. You can select from a variety of print sizes and frame options. Add a decidedly Western flair by pairing these prints with your favorite cowhide rug or leather couch.

Artfully Walls is the perfect destination for those who don’t know where to start their search for high-quality, wall-enhancing prints. It features a huge volume of works from a trove of emerging artists worldwide. If a high level of choice overwhelms you, or you simply want an expert’s opinion, take advantage of Artfully Walls’ collections of ready-to-hang art, curated by designers and industry professionals. Louisa Tratalos, founder of British interior design brand Colours of Arley, has an Artfully Walls collection that includes this print featuring colorful, Scandinavian-style architecture by Dutch photographer Sander Groenendijk. Or browse picks selected by Justin Huxol of Huxhux Designs, including this whimsical “sponge cake” photo by Julie Vielvoije.

#4752. Jennifer Lawrence’s Hair Care Brand Launch Faced Public Scrutiny—But How Do the Products Actually Perform?

I tested Mes° Beauty for two weeks to find out.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

When Jennifer Lawrence joined Instagram in September, fans rejoiced at the idea of seeing more content from the actress known for her sarcastic humor and likable authenticity. What we didn’t see coming was the launch of her new hair care brand Mes° Beauty (pronounced “mess”) and the public backlash that followed.

In an already oversaturated beauty market, celebrity brands are a dime a dozen, and the announcement of Mes° Beauty didn’t exactly land well with the public. “She saw the numbers Rihanna, Selena Gomez, and Hailey Bieber were pulling in, and suddenly decided to join Instagram, too. Not necessarily to connect with her audience, but perhaps to tap into the same commercial machine and sell us even more stuff,” wrote one Instagram commenter.

JLaw teamed up with Jasmina Aganovic, founder of biotech beauty company Arcaea Labs, to formulate the brand’s hair care. As they say, the proof is in the pudding, so when I was sent all three products in a PR mailer, I knew I wanted to put them to the test.

Read my full, honest review of Mes° Beauty’s hair mask, serum, and volume mist below.

An intensive repair mask designed to be applied to dry hair anytime before washing. The milky-colored mask has a silky yet sticky, gelatin-like consistency that clings to your hair as you apply it. According to the brand, the mask prevents breakage and wash-day protein loss and protects the hair’s lipid barrier.

The Multitask Repair Mask differs from other hair masks because you apply it before shampooing and can leave it on for five minutes or overnight. With such a wide treatment time, it might take some trial and error to find the “sweet spot” for your hair type. During my testing, I applied a generous coat of the mask 5 to 10 minutes before shampooing. The second time, I tried applying a thinner coat of the mask, then pinned my hair up with a claw clip for about two hours before rinsing it out. The longer you wear it, the better the results. I would recommend applying a light coat before going about your day; that way, the scent isn’t overpowering and it won’t drip on your clothes.

After just two uses, my hair looked shinier and felt more hydrated after styling. As someone who rarely plans my hair care routine ahead of time, I appreciate that I can apply the mask just five minutes before I hop in the shower and still get noticeable results.

Although Mes° says the mask doubles as a styler for a glossy wet-hair look, I wouldn’t use it in that way. I think the product's consistency is too sticky and would be uncomfortable and messy (literally) to wear all day.

Some reviewers have mentioned a slightly off-putting smell. While the scent doesn’t bother me (it smells like a light, musky fragrance), it may not be for everyone. If I’m paying $52 for a hair mask, it would be nice to have a luxurious fragrance to add to the experience. If a brand is going to do musk, really lean into it with notes of sandalwood, amber, or patchouli.

The packaging also makes the product difficult to use. In the mailer I received, the mask comes in a GoGo Squeez-like pouch that you’re supposed to empty into the plastic tub. However, dipping my fingers into the tub felt clumsy, and next time I would just dispense directly from the pouch.

A bi-phase serum that smooths frizz, restores shine, and provides heat protection up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. The “bi-phase” claim comes from combining a lightweight oil and a serum in the formula. After touching it, applying it, and letting it sit in my hair for a few days, I think calling it a serum is misleading. The consistency and the way it applies are much more like a hair oil.

On day two hair, I warmed two drops of the Off-Duty Restyling Serum between my palms, and worked it through my strands. I have very thick, straight, shoulder-length hair, so when I applied the serum up through my mid-lengths, it was way too oily. I don’t know if I would use it to restyle my hair unless I was planning to use a hot tool.

I also tested the serum as a finishing product, applying it to my ends after blow-drying. I found this to be the most effective way to use the product on my hair type.

Overall, the Off-Duty Restyling Serum doesn’t make much sense to me. What’s the point of having heat protection if it’s made for “reshaping yesterday’s style?” Are we going back in with more heat? To me, that sounds like an extra step in my morning routine that I do not have the time or patience for.

On days when I wash and blow-dry my hair, I like using a tiny amount of the serum just on my ends, and I've found it dries down nicely and leaves my hair soft and touchable. That said, I own other lightweight hair oils that work just as well for a fraction of the price—like FromLabs’ Protein Capsule Hair Repair Oil. If you have fine, wavy, or curly hair, the Off-Duty Serum may work better for you.

A lightweight spray that reduces scalp oiliness for lasting lift. Instead of creating gritty texture or absorbing excess oil like a dry shampoo, the Good Roots mist helps balance the scalp microbiome to produce less oil at the roots, extending the time until your next wash.

Over the past two weeks, I tested the Good Roots mist in three ways: applying it to damp hair before blow-drying, applying it to damp hair before air-drying, and applying it to dry day-two and day-three hair.

After about five uses of trial and error, I found it worked best when I applied it to my clean, damp roots and blow-dried. The heat felt like it helped dry down and “activate” the mist, whereas letting my hair air-dry didn’t produce much volume.

Pro-Tip: Be sure to hold the bottle about a foot away for even misting. The applicator pump doesn’t produce a fine spritz, and it took me a few uses to get that right.

After two weeks of testing, the Good Roots Volume Mist is my favorite of the trio. Two key ingredients, the proprietary Arc-5 Technology and the Mediterranean microalgae, help support a balanced scalp, keeping your hair fresher longer. With consistent use, the Good Roots mist extended my time between hair washes—I typically wash every other day, but I was able to go a third day. Plus, the Juniperus virginiana oil in the formula has a fresh, woody scent that reminds me of a fancy sea salt spray.

I also like that the mist doesn’t make my hair feel super gritty or textured the way a dry shampoo might. That said, I have other dry shampoo products that do a lot more heavy lifting than this volume mist. If I’m looking to achieve noticeable volume and lift in my thick hair, the Good Roots mist doesn’t cut it.

My general critique of Mes° Beauty is that the products are not very intuitive. They seem straightforward, but the brand doesn’t give great direction on how to get the most out of them. After the first one or two uses, you may feel they barely do anything at all. But if you learn how to use them properly when styling your hair, they can perform fairly well.

Mes° is supposed to be about “Less time fixing your hair. More time living,” but in reality, achieving that effortlessly chic, tousled look requires a fair bit of effort. In my opinion, this lineup is much more suited to someone who blows out or flat irons or curls their hair once or twice a week and wants to extend their style. For my hair type, these products don’t fit into my routine in a way that makes sense, but if you have fine and/or wavy hair, they might work better for you.

Curious about my other hair standbys? They’re currently $30 and under—and make for excellent beauty gift ideas for your loved ones for the upcoming holiday season.

#4751. Hyundai is overhauling the Kona, and it looks like it may still be offered as an EV after all

Hyundai is skipping the typical mid-cycle refresh and plans to launch a completely redesigned Kona, with a sleek new style and an updated high-tech interior.

It’s been nearly four years since Hyundai introduced the second-generation Kona, meaning, like most of its models, the compact SUV was expected to receive a mid-cycle refresh.

Hyundai is apparently going straight to the third-generation model instead. Earlier this year, early-stage prototypes were spotted in Korea that looked much boxier and more rugged than the current Kona.

Since then, several test mules have been captured testing in the US, Europe, and other regions, confirming the Kona will adopt a more upright, traditional SUV design similar to the new Santa Fe, Palisade, and Tucson.

The wider, more powerful design appears to draw inspiration from Hyundai’s off-road Crater Concept, revealed at the LA Auto Show last year.

Hyundai said the off-road SUV Concept was a preview of the “next evolution” of its Extreme Rugged Terrain (XRT) vehicles, such as the IONIQ 5 XRT and Palisade XRT Pro. Is the Kona next in line to receive the XRT treatment?

A post shared by SHORTS CAR (@shorts_car)

Apparent leaked images from a few months ago revealed a design that looked like a mashup of the Crater Concept and IONIQ 5, with pixelated lighting and a clamshell hood.

Most recently, the third-gen Hyundai Kona, codenamed “SX3,” was spotted disguised in a parking garage in Korea. The images were sent to ShortsCar, revealing the new Kona’s wheel design.

While earlier reports suggested Hyundai planned to drop the all-electric Kona variant and would only offer gas and hybrid versions, the prototype captured in Korea is expected to be the EV model. However, Hyundai has yet to confirm powertrain or battery specs.

The updates are even more evident on the inside. Previous spy images appeared to show the third-gen Hyundai Kona running Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, like the IONIQ 3.

In the IONIQ 3, Hyundai offers a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.

Like the current model, the third-gen Kona is expected to be available with fully electric (EV), hybrid, and gas-powered powertrains.

While Hyundai skipped the 2026 Kona EV, the electric version could return in 2027 or 2028 when the third-generation model is expected to arrive.

The hybrid version will likely use the same 1.6L hybrid engine as the new Seltos, while the EV variant could offer similar powertrain and battery options to the IONIQ 3.

The IONIQ 3 is available with two battery packs in Europe and the UK: 42 kWh and 61 kWh, offering WLTP ranges of up to 213 miles (344 km) and 308 miles (497 km), respectively.

#4750. 10 Best Storage Beds, As Told and Tested by AD’s Editors (2026)

When you're short on space (or even if you're not), having an extra set of drawers on hand is a huge boon for small bedrooms. That's where the best storage beds come in. I'm all about bedroom furniture that does more for your sleep setup, so I gathered up a few favorites from the AD staff. These storage bed picks include sleek, streamlined designs with completely concealed side storage, queen- and king-size beds with pullouts at the footboard, and more. Each one stows generously while you sleep.

A storage bed frame need not be ugly, even if function is the whole point of buying one. In fact, I tapped other editors and we found impressive wooden beds from Thuma and West Elm, the upholstered storage beds of our minimalist dreams from Saatva, Article, and Sundays, and a lilac velvet showpiece from CB2 for anyone who wants their storage bed to be the loudest thing in the room. The market has our back on this one, especially for those of us living in shoebox bedrooms where a queen bed barely fits, let alone a nightstand (the luxury). Below are the 10 storage beds I considered up to snuff, with editor commentary.

All prices in this article reflect queen-size beds unless otherwise noted.

All prices in this article reflect queen-size beds unless otherwise noted.

Bed frame reviewer: Kate McGregor, contributor

What attracted you to this bed frame? Like any girl living in New York in her mid-20s, I have a lot of stuff. And while I have ample closet space (a rarity), I like a certain level of type-A organization. Closed or hidden storage is key, and I didn’t want to fill my precious closet space with off-season sweaters and formalwear I reach for once a year. Enter: a platform storage bed. Not taking up any extra square footage was key, or else I would have bought a trunk or bookcase like my mother suggested. I had several coworkers who swore by Saatva’s mattresses for both quality and comfort, so investing in their furniture felt like a natural next step. The Halle bed frame is one of their more minimal silhouettes that I knew would suit my ever-evolving design style.

What was the delivery and assembly like? Delivery and assembly were a breeze. The team gave me an hour's notice before arriving, so I could prep my space (aka move my Amazon bed frame out of the way and vacuum). Assembly took about an hour, and the three-man team was incredibly efficient. They checked in with me multiple times throughout the process to ensure they got the placement exactly right. Afterward, they left with all the trash and packaging in tow, and they even helped me place my 150-pound mattress back onto the new frame.

Are there any standout features? The lift mechanism is really much smoother than I'd expected. Durable linen handles ensure that I'm never fighting for grip on the base. If I'm really feeling it, I can lift the base with one hand to access the storage below.

What’s your bedroom design, and how does this storage bed align with your aesthetic? My bedroom is quite minimal—jute rug, dark wood dresser, cream linen curtains. I change my bedding at every whim, so I wanted a bed frame that wouldn't take up too much attention from my gingham sheets and block-printed quilt. The beige linen frame does just that, it serves as a neutral backdrop for whatever bedding layers I choose.

Did the bed frame live up to your expectations? Yes, and then some. Over the last eight months, this bed has remained sturdy, and without being too dramatic, it has revolutionized my apartment’s storage. Christmas garlands, high heels, and even craft supplies have all found a home in the spacious cavity. Plus, the raised base keeps all of my belongings off the ground. The linen fabric has softened a bit with age, especially on the headboard and handles that I’m touching more frequently than the frame. The lift mechanisms are easy to use and lock while lifted, allowing me to maneuver in the storage space without holding the bed up. The lift even handles my 150-pound mattress with ease, not even creasing a pillow.

How would you rate the sturdiness of this bed frame on a scale of 1–10? The sturdiness is a 9/10—I dock it a point only because I pushed my bed frame and it shifted a bit away from the storage base. Otherwise, there's no movement, creaking, or stability issues, even as I toss and turn.

To truly give these recommendations on the best storage beds, I featured options that include a variety of price points, storage features, designs, and more to guide you on your own shopping journey. Read more on the key factors other writers and I kept in mind below:

Delivery and Assembly: The last thing you want is to wait months for your bed frame to help you organize (and elevate) your space. We selected options that offer reasonable shipping windows (usually within one month from placing your order to its arrival at your home) as well as white glove delivery to help set up the storage bed in your desired room, or a frame simple enough to assemble yourself.

Design: A big passion of ours at AD is finding furniture that is not only functional but is also not an eyesore. We skipped clunky bed frames and included pieces that can sit comfortably anywhere in modern and minimalist bedrooms and beyond.

Size: Our editors tested a mix of queen and king sizes, and prices in this story reflect queens. We looked for picks that come in a range of sizes to accommodate any space. Keep in mind that storage beds often have features like pull-out drawers and lift-up bases, so be sure to measure your space and compare it to your desired storage bed's dimensions to ensure the bed can open properly in your bedroom.

Storage Features: The storage bed you select should align with your space. If you're tight on floor space, consider a storage bed that lifts up. If you have low ceilings, consider a storage bed that has drawers underneath.

Durability: We tested storage beds by sleeping on them night after night, taking notice of any factors like creakiness or wobbliness. We also looked for options with high-quality materials like fine upholstery and solid wood that are designed to last.

Price: Storage beds run from a few hundred dollars to well over $2,000, and our picks span that whole range. While the price isn't always the biggest indicator of quality, materials like bouclé and solid wood are usually found in more high-end storage beds.

What Are the Different Types of Storage Beds?

Lift-up beds: Also called an "ottoman bed," this is a model where the mattress base lifts up with the aid of gas struts (pressurized cylinders that do most of the lifting for you), which retailers often call hydraulic lifts. This typically offers the most room out of the storage bed options.

Drawer beds: Fairly self-explanatory: drawers (either under, alongside, or at the foot of the bed) are this frame’s storage approach.

Headboard storage beds: A headboard storage bed draws from mid-century styles, where built-in shelves or nightstands create storage opportunities. This is a good option if what you need to store is also aesthetically pleasing.

Cubby beds: Instead of drawers, these cubbies are open shelving solutions underneath the bed frame, particularly suitable for holding books if you’re looking for a stylish way to create a bedroom library.

What’s a “Hydraulic Lift” in a Storage Bed?

When your storage bed has interior storage (in other words, when you lift the mattress base upward to access its storage), it needs a lift mechanism to make it possible for you to lift the bed without breaking your back, and to keep the slatted frame upright while you lift your items in and out. Most use gas struts, though you'll often see them sold as hydraulic. If your storage bed has interior storage and no lift, you will collapse yourself and ultimately be pancaked by your own sleep-and-store investment.

What Features Should I Look for in the Best Storage Beds?

A good storage bed, in our opinion, doesn't look like a storage bed. It looks like a regular bed. It's crafted from, ideally, kiln-dried hardwood, it has a slatted base so you don't need to bother with a box spring, and it has non-sticky drawers (thank you, Thuma) or a lift mechanism to help with the lifting of interior storage (thank you, Saatva). Look for a solid wood base, linen upholstery, and invest in some vacuum-sealed bags. I live by these.

You're primarily searching for durability and space in storage bed models. Look for frames made from solid wood since this type of material is typically sturdy and long-lasting. A lift mechanism makes storage more accessible without back-breaking exercises. While upholstered beds are a popular favorite, make sure what lies beneath the textile is also going to stand the test of time.

#4748. 7 Running Shorts for Women That WH Editors Love

Editor-tested picks built for comfort, pockets, and sweat control.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

There’s nothing more humiliating than having a huge sweat stain on your butt after strenuous mile repeats—been there, done that. A good run is supposed to lift your mood, not bring you down, so finding the best running shorts to keep the endorphins flowing (and your butt dry) is essential.

Not all workout shorts are made the same. Some offer more compression, while others are less restrictive and have convenient features like pockets—the holy grail! “You need a place to carry all your resources—pockets are a non-negotiable for running gels, electrolytes, phone, wallet, and keys,” says New York-based running coach and personal trainer Amanda Katz, NASM-CPT.

While many athletic shorts can be used for different purposes, running shorts usually have a built-in interior liner, sweat-wicking material, and a nonconstrictive design to keep you cool and comfortable as you rack up mileage in your sleek running shoes.

I researched and gathered the best running shorts from a running coach and editors who’ve personally tested them. Whether you’re training for a marathon or are a hobby jogger, all the shorts I picked are from trusted activewear and athleisure brands that will benefit you in the long run (literally). Ready to find out more about the best running shorts for women? Keep scrolling.

After testing countless pairs of running shorts over the years, the Hotty Hot High-Rise Lined Short from Lululemon is my fave for its sweat-wicking fabric and comfortable fit. The polyester blend wicks away sweat, prevents cling, and promotes airflow while running. The loose, flowy fit keeps me cool, while a built-in interior liner adds lightweight coverage and support without bulk.

The side pockets are small, but hold small essentials like a credit card, key, or energy gels for long runs. The leg openings are spacious, allowing for a full range of motion, and an adjustable drawstring secures the waistband for a customizable fit. Want to hit the road at the crack of dawn or at night? No sweat; reflective detailing improves visibility in dark or dim light, making early morning or evening runs safer.

I appreciate the 4-inch length, given I prefer more coverage, but a 2.5-inch length is available if you prefer a shorter fit. WH associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian, NASM-CPT, is also a fan of the fit and vast color palette. “They never ride up or move around, which is hard to find in a running short,” she says. With tons of colors and sizes to choose from, you can't go wrong.

New Balance is a top brand in the running world, and the RC Short is one of my faves. It runs slightly big, but I love the extra breathing room during a sweat session.

The lightweight, flowy construction uses the brand’s quick-drying tech fabric (a polyester and spandex blend) to wick moisture from the skin. The breathable design promotes tons of airflow, creating a cooling effect while I run—especially ideal during scorching hot summer runs.

The seamless, interior lining reduces chafing and irritation, while the waistband features an adjustable drawstring to customize the fit. It’s also not too tight—some liners can feel like you’re wearing a diaper (hate). As for storage, there’s a back pocket for securing small running essentials and even tiny snacks like a granola bar when you’re on the move.

A pair of high cut shorts, such as the Alo Match Point Short, is a running staple. The high-cut at the thighs keeps things perfectly airy and flowy for optimal coolness when I get overheated, more so than the Lululemon Hotty Hot Short.

This construction, paired with its moisture-wicking polyester fabric, creates the perfect breathable running shorts. While it’s a bit short at just over two inches, there’s still great coverage with a built-in brief, and I find it doesn’t show too much skin.

WH style contributor Lily Wolhner also appreciates this loose style for various workouts. “My favorite part about this short is that it’s never clingy, so it doesn’t ride up the thigh or need constant re-adjusting while you’re working out,” Wolhner says. “I’ve worn it for months and recently tested it during a 45-minute strength and HIIT workout, as well as an hour-long cross-training workout—I never felt over-exposed or uncomfortable in it.”

By the looks of the elastic waistband, I expected it to dig into my skin—wrong. It felt comfortable, although it’s important to note this short does run big, so I suggest sizing down.

We love a two-for-one, and this short from Brooks is ideal for both trail running and running at the gym. It has light compression with a built-in tight liner that doesn’t sacrifice mobility.

The mega-durable polyester fabric resists tears and moisture, which makes it ideal for trail running in tough terrain. “I love the high waist, the zipper pocket to carry my keys, and the tight shorts under a looser short aesthetic,” Katz says.

Two waistband pockets are impressively large and can even fit a water flask, so you can always stay hydrated during your jogs.

I personally don’t love compression-lined shorts because I like to feel totally free, but if you prefer extra coverage and double layers, this short is ideal.

If you want a no-frills pair of shorts at an affordable price point that will stand the test of time, the Under Armour Play Up 3.0 belongs in your running gear collection. I’ve owned multiple pairs for years in eye-catching colors, and they’re still in good condition with no pills—even after dozens of runs and wash cycles.

The lightweight knit fabric made from smooth polyester has an anti-pill finish for extra durability, and is impressively comfy. Plus, it hides embarrassing sweat stains post-run, despite the slightly thicker material.

The waistband uses a wide elastic band that provides a secure fit without any adjustable features. However, I find it still fits roomy and allows for a full range of motion.

It includes deep side pockets but no enclosure, so I don’t recommend stashing anything super important besides fuel, like energy gels. I wear it the most for shorter, mid-distance runs and whenever I want to add a pop of color—it has 21 color options!

I usually don’t gravitate toward compression shorts since I don’t like feeling constricted, but the Athleta Salutation Stash 5-Inch Short offers the perfect amount of tightness. It hugs my thighs with gentle compression, while the high-rise waistband distributes pressure evenly for a secure fit without digging in. Plus, the two deep side pockets offer convenient storage for longer runs.

The smooth, double-knit fabric is buttery-soft and offers great coverage. While on the thicker side, it conceals sweat stains well—a huge win during long-haul runs. I wouldn’t say it feels the most breathable compared to other shorts in this guide, but the nylon and lycra blend wicks away sweat and dries fast.

Another huge selling point? The fabric’s UPF 50 protection, which prevents UV radiation from scorching your thighs. This is my favorite feature as someone fair-skinned and prone to nasty sunburns (IYKYK). Aside from its fabric, I love that it has a matching jacket for a coordinated workout set.

Tracksmith’s Van Cortlandt Shorts combine retro styling with a performance-driven design that makes them a winner both on and off the track. It’s made from a lightweight mesh fabric to maximize airflow, paired with an antimicrobial finish to help combat odor by wicking away sweat and limiting bacteria buildup during intense runs.

After summer runs when I’m dripping with sweat, I noticed zero smell—and that the short dries at the speed of light.

Like our best overall, it’s quite short at 2.5 inches, so if you prefer a longer style, you should look to other styles in this guide. On the flip side, it doesn’t disrupt my range of motion during speed work or long runs. As for fit, I found it runs true to size, but make sure to consult the size chart as always.

Running shorts with sweat-wicking fabric are the way to go, Katz says. Most shorts use a blend of polyester, spandex, and/or nylon, which lifts moisture from the skin while staying flexible during movement. Based on testing, it’s best to avoid cotton since it doesn’t dry nearly as fast and clings to the skin when wet.

It’s important to determine what kind of rise and inseam you desire. High-waisted running shorts offer more coverage and tummy control, while a mid-rise waist sits right at the hips. Ultimately, what you find most flattering for your body type is the best option.

The inseam is the length from the crotch to the bottom. A longer length will show less skin but may disrupt the range of motion, while some running shorts favorites, like the Lululemon Hotty Hot High-Rise Lined Short, offer a 2.5-inch option if you like a mini fit.

As for an interior liner or compression, this will make running shorts fit more snugly. “Compression is a matter of preference, but the goal in this material is to boost recovery,” says Katz. If you want a less constrictive fit, it’s probably best to avoid that feature.

In addition to my own testing, Women’s Health associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian, NASM-CPT also extensively tested tons of running shorts to determine whether or not they’re the real deal. Each pair was worn during training runs or races for anywhere from three weeks to even three years to see how they performed and held up.

Essential features considered were materials, inseam, pockets, durability, and adjustability. Additionally, I asked a running coach for their go-to running shorts and guidance on how they should fit.

#4747. Tesla stops selling every Cybertruck except the $109,990 Cyberbeast

Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.

The Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected. So the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today costs $109,990, up 57% from $69,990 in early August.

Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator shows today with a Los Angeles delivery address:

A week ago, the Cyberbeast cost $102,490. Before that, it was $99,990. That’s a $10,000 (10%) increase in about a week on a truck that hasn’t changed: 320 miles of estimated range, 11,000 lbs of towing, and 0-60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

On November 6, the same day Elon Musk announced the end of Cybertruck production, Tesla raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. That made the $92,490 Premium AWD the entry point. Now it’s gone too, with no announcement. The configurator just stopped letting you pick it.

New inventory isn’t an alternative either. When we checked, Tesla’s inventory search showed no new Cybertrucks within 200 miles of Los Angeles.

This comes two days after Musk extended Cybertruck production through the end of summer 2027 to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” On Monday, he claimed the order rate “far exceeds” production and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

If there really is a backlog, cutting off the two cheaper trims is one way to cap it before the line shuts down. It also pushes whatever demand is left toward the most expensive, highest-margin version of the truck.

But the sales data doesn’t describe a truck with a demand problem in the other direction. We estimate Tesla delivered 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks in Q3, a pace of about 30,000 a year on a line with more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. And in February, Tesla was offering a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.”

That’s $50,000 less than the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today. Nine months later.

Some of those $59,990 buyers are still waiting on delivery dates pushed into 2027. Tesla hasn’t said whether their orders, or any other Dual Motor and Premium orders in the queue, will be built before production ends.

Unlike the thousands of $59k CT orders that may never get manufactured I can guarantee that every high margin $110k CyberBeast order will be delivered before production ends.

This is the wind-down playbook, and it’s moving faster than I expected. Announce the end, raise prices, pull the cheaper trims, and sell the last trucks in their most expensive form. Tesla is squeezing as much as it can out of every remaining Cybertruck.

I don’t blame Tesla for wanting margin on a program it’s walking away from. But it makes the “order backlog” talk look like what we said it was: an end-of-life rush Tesla created by announcing the end, now being monetized with a $109,990 sticker. Not great for anyone who was told in 2019 that this truck would start at $39,900, or that the tri-motor version would cost $69,900.

If you want a Cybertruck that isn’t a Cyberbeast, you’re now shopping used. And I’d keep an eye on used prices, because a truck that’s going out of production with no cheaper new option could hold its value better than it has over the last two years.

#4746. The 10 Best Fitness Trackers, Tested by Our Fitness and Tech Experts

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Our fitness team recommends trackers from Garmin, Apple, and Suunto.

NOT SURE WHAT fitness tracker is right for you? You've come to the right place. We've been wearing and documenting fitness trackers as far back as 2015, when we reviewed the very first Apple Watch. We started cross-comparing fitness trackers as early as 2017, when we broke down the best fitness trackers for activities like strength training, running, hiking, golf, and more. Now in 2026, we're more dialed into the state of fitness trackers than ever before as nearly all our editors are wearing some sort of device on a daily basis.

On the most basic level, the best fitness trackers offer GPS connectivity to help you stay on your training course and basic activity tracking. Newer iterations of fitness trackers include advanced smartwatches that can do anything from tracking your archery workout to detecting a heart attack, as well as (our personal favorite) smart rings. Smart rings pack a ton (no literally, an absurd amount) of sleep/stress stats and workout/health information into a tiny package you wear on your finger 24/7.

Depending on what your health and fitness goals are (like losing weight, improving your sleep, or cutting time off your mile PR), the best fitness trackers can help you identify where your training is lacking, optimize your stress levels, improve your recovery time, and streamline your training sessions and daily wellness habits.

As the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, it’s my job to test the latest and greatest fitness trackers. I am supported in this effort by my fellow editors like Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S., Grooming Editor Sean Zucker, Senior Gear Editor Ryan Brower, and Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM. We have put countless fitness trackers through the gauntlet and evaluated models on accuracy, design, durability, and price. We also paid close attention to comfort, ease of use, syncing with our favorite apps, and their ability to meet our standards for any activity.

We update our lineup of fitness trackers often, so you can expect up-to-date information that takes into account the latest fitness tracker releases.

If you want a basic level fitness tracker, the Whoop PEAK membership with its new 5.0 band may be your answer. Men’s Health Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. backs this device for that reason. “Simplicity is what works here, because it's reliable, has great battery life, and I don't need to think about it,” he says. The Whoop 5.0 Band is a fitness tracker band, which means though it’s still decently functional, it does not have a display like most wrist devices. It tracks all of your data in the corresponding phone app, but it’s worth noting, you cannot see the data directly on your wrist.

If you like the no-frills appearance, the Whoop 5.0 can definitely accomplish most of your tracking needs. “Whoop's activity sensing has improved over the years and continues to take steps,” says Samuel. It can track anything from running, cycling, and rowing to weightlifting, yoga, soccer, and even massage therapy. From our personal experience with Whoop, we love how it fits on the wrist. It is one of the more comfortable fitness trackers we’ve worn—the strap has a soft back, is woven with microfilament yarn, and can also be easily adjusted.

Unfortunately, Samuel had some qualms with the heart rate monitoring. “The device isn't tremendously accurate in terms of tracking heart rate, which is important to note,” he says. “In general, note that whatever [Whoop] is telling you about heart rate, it's almost always overshooting.” This can be an issue because a lot of the other tracking metrics (calories, activity, etc.) are based around heart rate. However, if you just want something basic to wear on your wrist, count your steps, and give you a general look into your health and workouts, Whoop 5.0 Band with the Peak membership will do just that.

Oura was a pioneer in the smart ring space, and it’s still the best smart ring we’ve tested to date (and we’ve tested a lot). Multiple editors have been wearing an Oura Ring for the last ten years and can attest that each new iteration outkicks the competition. This particular release updated a few physical features: Oura shifted to a fully titanium build (vs. a titanium exterior, epoxy interior), added smaller and larger sizes, and ditched its three-nodule sensor design. This latest model eliminates the nodules that used to be on the inside of the ring and pinch into my finger on the Oura Ring 3. Those aren't required anymore with the new tech, so that is a huge improvement over the past model.

The battery can also last up to eight days now, instead of just seven. And the updated software is available on all models, new and old. While Oura has always offered heart rate monitoring, the new software now features automatic heart rate monitoring, allowing you to detect and track your workout stats without hitting the “Record HR workout” button. This automatic detection feature also lends itself to workout monitoring for over 40 activities (a new capability compared to the past, solely cardio-focused tracking that Oura offered).

The daytime stress features have also gotten an improvement—one of our favorites is illness detection. The Oura Ring 5 can detect changes in your stress stats and body temperature that may indicate an illness before you feel the entirety of the symptoms. A couple of months ago, one editor felt a slight earache when they woke up, and Oura called out they may have a cold coming on. The next day, that cold had arrived. It’s not always entirely accurate like this—there have been a few times the Oura Ring has said we were getting sick when it was actually just a hangover (oops).

Even as Oura lovers, we’d be remiss not to call out one of the downsides to the product: In order to attain full use of the Oura Ring, you need to pay a monthly subscription fee of $5.99 (or $69.99 per year). There are other smart rings in the space that don’t require any fee (shout out to our second favorite product, the Ultrahuman ring), but with the updated technology and consistent top-of-the-line features, we deem the extra $69.99 per year a pretty minimal price to pay.

For the most style-conscious users, the company also released a Ceramic version of the Oura Ring 4, which offers a unique look and additional color options.

Read More: Our Hands-On Test of the Oura Ring 5

Adventurers, look this way. We’re not exaggerating when we say this is the most rugged fitness tracker we have tested. The Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED is packed with technology and has a thick face made for trail hikes, rock climbing, and even swimming (it’s water rated up to 100 meters). According to Men’s Health contributor Korin Miller, this Garmin can take a beating. “I accidentally banged it into several doorways and even scraped it against a kettlebell during a clumsy gym moment—it still looks brand new,” Miller says.

In addition to its outwardly masculine look and durable design, the technology here is super simple to navigate, which can’t be said for all fitness trackers. Though there’s no touchscreen, Miller had the five buttons figured out within just a few minutes of receiving the product. And while you can track up to 30 different workout types, Miller praises the display for the easy-to-digest layout outside of workout mode. “The 390-by-390-pixel AMOLED display resolution is sharp and bright, allowing Garmin to jam a lot of stats on the home screen. At a glance, you can see your step count, heart rate, weather, date, time, and more. It’s arranged smartly in a way to deliver plenty of information without feeling overwhelming,” she says.

But one of our favorite features? Garmin prioritizes a wind-down time, switching from a jam-packed interface to just a clock during the time you are typically sleeping (which you note during set-up). It’s worth mentioning that in order to be this rugged and durable, the Garmin Instinct 3 is also quite heavy at 53 grams. But if you’re going hard on the trails, there’s no better wrist partner.

Read More: Our Hands-On Test of the Garmin Instinct 3

At this cost, you’d expect a simple appearance, no touchscreen, and limited functionality. However, the Google Pixel Watch 5 has a beautiful, easy-to-navigate touchscreen, a smooth design, and almost all the metrics you’d get on a more high-end device.

Google puts a big emphasis on overall wellness rather than just fitness tracking, focusing on breathing and stress management. “This is a very underrated device and it's gotten more accurate with the third edition,” says Samuel. “The breathing exercises don't reinvent the wheel, but the presentation is solid and the timing is good. Overall, in this market, there's a lot we don't fully understand about stress levels, and some of the algorithms are simplistic. But Google has smartly gotten us thinking about how we feel, and that's a good thing.”

If this watch tracks stress, readiness, and sleep, what are the limitations of this budget-friendly device? Well, it doesn’t offer as many workout modes as most other fitness trackers, clocking in at just 41 options. You also have to charge it every day, and it’s only compatible with Android devices. But for such a clean, aesthetic appearance and great individual wellness metrics, we definitely consider this fitness tracker a steal.

Most fitness trackers carry a hefty price tag, so if you’re in the market but not looking to sell out on this particular accessory, the Suunto Race S is the best value you’ll find. With a high definition AMOLED touchscreen, over 95 sport modes, and a water rating up to 50m, the specs here are just as good as you’ll find on many high-end fitness trackers. The AMOLED display on this watch is fantastic for its compact design. And personally, I think the Suunto Race S is superior to the larger model.

A lot of fitness trackers in this price range (around $350) offer only more basic tracking, like steps and calories burned. That’s not the case here, there is more to this fitness watch than just a run tracker—there are workouts and other great fitness insights, like HRV, sleep monitoring, activity tracking and race pacing. Sure, it's not as powerful as a top-of-the-line Garmin, but it gets the job done and brings great value.

Let’s chat about some of those features. Sleep tracking is having a moment and the Suunto Race S can track your sleep duration, timing, deep sleep, light sleep, heart rate, REM and HRV from sleep. One downside here? Wearing a watch to bed isn’t for everyone. Another cool feature worth digging into is race pacing. If you’re training for an upcoming marathon (or just life), the Race Pacer can help keep you on track when the mid-long run rut strikes. Overall, this is a great budget-friendly find—just note that if you opt for the titanium version over the stainless steel version, that will hike the price up by $120 (which makes it not as budget-friendly).

Apple fans already know how great the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is. It features a large, durable aerospace-grade titanium body built for outdoor adventure. It’s water-rated up to 100m and boasts dual-frequency GPS. What’s that do for you exactly? It offers much more accurate tracking in tough environments (like densely populated cities, mountain terrain, and forests)—great for trail runners and climbers.

Apple has always been at the top of the game for fitness tracking. The Ultra 4 offers all the typical metrics of the older Apple Watch models—activity rings, over 60 workout modes, blood oxygen, ECG, etc. But the Ultra 4 can be used as a dive computer, an emergency siren, and a compass that retraces your steps (ideal for those prone to getting lost mid-hike).

A watch that can do this much won’t look dainty on the wrist, though. Men’s Health Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM wrapped everything up nicely here. “The new design overhauled the sensor, which is on the rear of the watch and sits against the wearer’s wrist. Even though the casing is still the same 49-millimeter size as previous versions of the device and the sensor takes up the same amount of space.” Williams continues, “There’s now more surface area for device-to-skin contact for ECG readings, a new, circular optical sensing array, and larger, more efficient LEDs for heart rate sensing.”

For us, the only real downside is that it’s a bit chunky on the wrist, but we’ll take it—the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is truly the full package for all iPhone users.

Read More: Our Hands-On Test of the Apple Watch Ultra 4

If you’ve ever been big into running, you’ve likely considered a Garmin watch. But the Garmin Fēnix 9 isn’t just great for run tracking—it tracks over 100 different types of workouts and can last up to 29 days on one charge. In addition to its functionality, the Garmin Fēnix 9 also boasts a high-end design. One of the thinner offerings in the way of chunky Garmins, this is the perfect fitness tracking watch for anyone who doesn’t want to wear anything too cumbersome on the wrist (plus it now comes in a 43mm size). This watch has everything that fitness tracking powerhouse Garmin has to offer packed into its low-profile casing.

One of the coolest offerings? Garmin has both an AMOLED and a solar-powered option. The solar-powered watch can extend the battery life even further, but the screen is not quite as bright as the AMOLED option. The solar watch also does not have a touchscreen like the AMOLED one, making it a bit less convenient to have to click through the features via buttons.

While the Garmin Fēnix 9 has the capabilities to track pretty much any metric you want tracked, the charging experience falls a bit short. While the battery can last up to 24 days in low-power mode, turning on GPS drops that to just under 24 hours of charge—a stark difference. Additionally, the charging cord is a bit short, so you might want to keep these USB-C charger extension cords on hand to charge your Garmin.

Overall, this is a sleek, all-in-one package with a unique (and modern) solar-powered option. If you don’t mind a bit of a sub-par charging experience, you can’t get more premium than the Garmin Fēnix 9.

No iPhone? No problem. The Galaxy Watch9 can go anywhere thanks to a large scratch-resistant screen and a strong titanium case. One of our favorite features is the advanced sleep coaching that analyzes your sleep habits, suggests what you can do to improve, and is even FDA-approved to detect sleep apnea. We also appreciate the body composition reader—in just a few seconds, the Galaxy Watch9 works to tell you your vitals, and even provides a body fat estimate. These stats are prone to inaccuracy (few home devices can accurately track body fat), but we give props to Samsung for trying to push metrics to another level.

The Galaxy Watch9 also delivers the features you expect in high-end smartwatches. That means accurate dual-frequency GPS specs and voice navigation. Nailing these (as Samsung does) is extra-critical, partly because the Galaxy Watch9 has some new competition for Android users (namely, from Google's Pixel Watch).

Thanks to several generations of trial and error and new AI health insights, the Galaxy Watch gets the edge as our preferred pick for Android owners. There are more health insights and data in this watch than most competitors. Once you grant the device access to your health insights on your phone, it will make recommendations on sleep, exercise, and overall health, after you choose what your own personal goals are. I appreciate the design as well, which looks more like a classic watch than other smartwatch options.

The array of features available and the materials used to craft the watch have been optimized a few times over, thus producing a seriously strong, long-lasting fitness tracker (and everyday smart watch) most users will be happy adding to their training arsenal.

When you’re just starting out, you probably want a no-fuss fitness tracker to help get your bearings. The G-Shock Move is easy to navigate and offers just enough tracking to get you started. Men’s Health Grooming and Commerce Editor Sean Zucker tested it out for himself and likes how easy it is for newbies. “Thankfully, where the watch really excels is where it’s most meant to be used—when you’re working out or going for a run,” Zucker says. “Its face has a simple design and navigating it was a breeze, even for someone as technologically challenged as myself. It was easy to switch between lap/route times, heart rate/zone, homepage, etc. while I was running with only a couple of clicks (the watch itself only has 4 buttons so I appreciate the simplified design).”

The G-Shock Move tracks all your basic needs: steps, running, walking, heart rate, blood oxygen, and even sleep recovery. Zucker also found it quite comfortable. “[It’s a] super comfortable watch, and handles sweat/rain with ease,” he says. “It doesn’t move around at all or get greasy after a long run/workout.” Though he did have a couple qualms with the functionality.

“Now, I’m not someone who likes to wear a watch, let alone a fitness watch, all of the time but I will if I have a few minutes or I’m planning out a run,” says Zucker. “I’ll check in on what I’ve done that week and unfortunately, the app doesn’t let you access any of that info unless your phone is currently connected, which is, in my professional opinion, quite annoying.” Another small downside, Zucker did mention he had a tough time with initial setup.

“It’s important to note that I am generally 100 years old and grumpy about this type of stuff, [but] still, the set up on this watch was a bit of a pain,” says Zucker. “There were a lot of ads (this extends to the app itself after you start using as well, very muddy).” If you can get past the setup and are okay with only being able to check past stats when you’re connected to the phone app, this is a great beginner-friendly tracker offering all the basic functions you need to kick off your fitness tracking journey.

Fitbit is back, with a vengeance. The Fitbit Air is the brand’s smallest and lightest tracker ever, weighing just 12 grams and featuring a design 25 percent smaller than the discontinued Luxe. Setup is simple through the new Google Health app, and the Air’s tracking features, including 24/7 heart rate, HRV, skin temperature, and sleep, run seamlessly in the background, with automatic workout detection and a reliable seven-day battery life.

What truly elevates the experience is the integration of Google’s Health Coach AI, available through a Google Health Premium subscription, which is included for those who already have Google One. Food logging is a surprise standout—you can snap a picture of your meal, and the app accurately breaks down the macros. While the core tracking functions are available without a subscription, the real value comes from the Premium features like AI coaching, deeper analytics, and adaptive plans. But you don’t need the membership for the basic features.

Some trade-offs to consider: The Air is screenless, so you can’t check notifications or your heart rate on the go, which may take some getting used to for smartwatch users. The default band can feel a bit stiff, and you charge it off-wrist. Still, the Fitbit Air is a compelling option for those who want minimalist, screenless health tracking without a hefty commitment.

At $99 with no required subscription, it’s an accessible entry point for anyone who wants comprehensive health data and a genuinely helpful AI coach, especially those seeking a distraction-free, streamlined alternative to full-featured smartwatches.

Read More: Our Full Review of the Google Fitbit Air

Fitness trackers started as mostly wrist devices—from step counters like the Fitbit to the original Apple Watch. Now, you can choose from an array of fitness tracking watches or smart rings, all of which track far more than just your fitness. While most of these devices offer similar capabilities, the design you choose—watch or ring—will depend on your own personal aesthetic.

Do you prefer the look of a fitness tracker watch? Do you find it more convenient to navigate all your stats on your wrist? Or do you like the look of a ring better and prefer the sleeker, more compact design? If so, are you also agreeable to the fact that you will need to visit your phone app to view all of your stats? Only you have the answers to these personal questions.

Fitness trackers don’t just track fitness anymore. Sure, your workouts are still a key part of what these devices do, but in addition they’re also tracking your sleep, heart rhythm patterns, blood oxygen levels, HRV, stress, and even caffeine consumption. Fitness trackers are more of an overall wellness tool than ever before.

That said, the type of fitness tracker you choose should weigh heavily on the way you intend to use it. If you’re just looking for insights into your sleep cycle, you’ll probably want a smart ring that’s fairly comfortable to wear to bed each night. If you’re training for a marathon, you may want a watch with a touchscreen that’s easy to navigate mid-run. This last part may be especially important: If you’re already using certain tracking apps that you love (let’s say, Apple Fitness for instance), you’ll want to make sure you find yourself a fitness tracker that is compatible with that app in particular.

The accuracy of a fitness tracker begins and ends with how precisely it tracks your heart rate (most other stats, with the exception of new hydration tracking features, are derived from this baseline data). This mark is as much about pure accuracy as it is about consistency of accuracy, which is key in helping you understand your own fitness trends. While some trackers tend to be more accurate than others, all of the trackers we included here were consistently accurate.

With the exception of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the Samsung Galaxy Watch9 (two fitness trackers that are equal parts smartwatch but have seen improvement in their battery life), the fitness trackers we tested are all designed to run for days (even weeks) on a single charge. We love a fitness tracker that needs minimal charging, and we also love a fitness tracker that can run for a long time when running its GPS mode. Two fitness trackers that surprised us when testing battery life include the Suunto Race S (up to 13 days on a single charge) and the Garmin Instinct 3 (21 days on a single charge when set to its most basic mode).

All fitness trackers are made to take a beating, but some are better designed than others. Look at case construction, screen construction, and for smart rings, material. The most advanced fitness trackers (smart rings included) are typically made with stainless steel, titanium, or another type of quality metal. For screens, sapphire glass is a premium spec to look for thanks to its high scratch resistance and strength.

Sometimes the most durable fitness tracker is unnecessary, though, especially if you are using it for pavement running. In fact, a plastic construction fitness tracker can be a much better choice for cardio-intensive activities like running and biking, since the material is going to be much lighter than stainless steel or titanium. On the flip side, if you are using your fitness tracker for strength training (or hiking or trail running), it would make sense to look for stronger materials.

#4744. You Know Animal-Print Rugs, But Do You Know Animal Pictorials? (2026)

The oldest known pile rug—pulled from a frozen tomb in Siberia in 1949—features a procession of 24 fallow deer and a parade of men on horseback. Some 2,500 years after its creation, animal illustrations are making their way back onto the floor. A serpent coils through the Snake and Pomegranate rug by Christopher Farr and Studio Shamshiri in Lucy Hale’s Los Angeles home, and a Tibetan tiger stretches across Demi Lovato’s modern farmhouse and Ethan Cook’s SoHo loft. These aren’t spots or stripes standing in for a neutral—they’re meant to be noticed and discussed. “Animal print is a texture; an animal motif is a story,” says AD100 designer Pavitra Rajaram, who recently designed Bahaar, an animal-themed rug in her Majnun collection for Jaipur Living. “I think people are tired of decoration that says nothing and are looking for objects that carry meaning.”

Rajaram is describing a literal animal rug, also known as an animal pictorial. These playful floor coverings often feature a bucolic scene of several animals or a single animal form woven into the textile, and they come in styles ranging from avant-garde and surrealist to Art Deco and folk-inspired.

“What we’re seeing now is a shift toward rugs where the whole animal is part of the design and has a role in the composition,” says Kerri Anne Besse, design director at rug brand Tumble. “The oversized, blown-up animal print feels dated.”

As for styling, Sophie Salata, head of brand at Vinterior, recommends that designers let the pictorials stand on their own. “I’d be inclined to treat the rug almost as a piece of art, allowing it to become a focal point rather than trying to make everything around it match,” she says. Pamela Marshall, creative director at artisanal rug brand Patterson Flynn, agrees with this approach: These designs are more than backdrops.

Reformation's nine-piece rug collection with Les Éditions de Tapis includes depictions of cats, swans, and tigers.

Recently, brands have been launching their own interpretations of animal pictorials. Last week, Reformation launched its first-ever home collection, a collaboration with Les Éditions de Tapis that features hand-drawn swans and cats. At Milan Design Week this year, Fornasetti launched a surrealist-inspired line of rugs with CC-Tapis depicting slithering serpents from the luxury designer’s archive. A few months earlier, Ruggable released its collaboration with Scalamandré to bring the upscale design house’s iconic zebras to more homes. And in October 2025, Nordic Knots launched its Swedish Grace collection, including the Grace 03 Fauna rug, which shows a wildlife scene. Looking further back, Beni’s serpent rugs have been a designer favorite since 2020.

One of the earlier examples of literal animal rugs is a collection between longstanding collaborators Patterson Flynn and AD100 designers Charlap Hyman & Herrero. It grew from a one-off rug into a full collection of graphic natural-and-black silhouettes that launched in 2018 and continues to expand. “Areas of inspiration for these come from Calder’s simplified animal forms, the surrealists’ play on scale, and 17th-century cabinets of curiosity, to name a few,” says Marshall, who credits Hyman’s “encyclopedic” design references for the originality. We would be remiss not to mention Diane von Furstenberg’s long-running collaboration with the Rug Company, which has been producing the iconic Climbing Leopard rug since 2005.

Rugs from Charlap Hyman & Herrero x Patterson Flynn’s collaboration.

The Rug Company x Diane von Furstenberg Climbing Leopard rug in emerald.

These rugs’ rich history might be part of their renewed appeal. Animals have been a subject for as long as people have made pictures. The oldest known figurative cave painting—found in Indonesia and dated to at least 51,200 years ago—shows a wild pig with three human figures.

“Animals have shaped our textiles and rugs for longer than we think,” says Bella Valenzia, founder of Pelican House, pointing out that animal forms have appeared in tapestries and wall coverings, and as functional home objects, such as pelt and hide rugs used for warmth and comfort, since the earliest days of humankind. “We like to think it is part of a wider return to folk-inspired, storytelling textiles, with a sense of nostalgia,” she adds. Pelican House’s rug Frith references the old English countryside, where horses have long been at the heart of rural life.

Various animals, real and mythical, carry their own significance across cultures, and their meaning can deeply influence a home’s design. For example, a pictorial of a lion, which signifies power in certain cultures, adds a very different element to a space than a fish, which can signify good luck, notes Jahanshah “Josh” Nazmiyal of Rug & Kilim. Veronica Renton, senior vintage and antiques specialist at 1stDibs, adds that peacocks often signal nobility and immortality.

Plenty of designers still reach for the originals: While the contemporary versions of these rugs are having a moment, their earlier counterparts remain relevant. “I particularly love antique Tibetan tiger rugs and Persian and Chinese rugs featuring guardian lions, dragons, and all manner of mythical beasts,” says Tiffany Duggan, founder of Studio Duggan.

The Tiger Rug by Studio Ashby in Sophie Ashby’s former home in London.

Where these rugs live in the home is likewise important. Naturally, the pieces work well in spaces that are meant to be playful, like nurseries and children’s rooms. For example, in this garden apartment designed by Rebecca Benichou and Florence Jallet of Batiik Studio, the Toulemonde Bochart Lion rug brings a spot of levity to a windowless craft room. In the bedroom of Kate Upton and Justin Verlander’s daughter, Genevieve, designed by John Ruggiero, the Doing Goods Blooming Black Bear Rug provides a spot of whimsy. For double the fun, designer Olivia Song put two animal rugs, the Doing Goods Pinky Lion and Pinky Leopard, in her nephew’s room in this Sag Harbor beach home.

That said, these rugs work in more adult spaces, too. “In the [primary] bedroom of one of our London projects, we used the beautiful Snake and Pomegranate rug,” says Duggan. “I love the way the snake weaves its way around the bed, creating a focal point and bringing a little humor and unexpected character to an otherwise calm space.”

Designer Rayman Boozer from Apartment 48 has a rug with a large tiger on it from the Rug Company in his own home. “Animal motifs can sometimes feel juvenile, but there’s something refreshing about bringing that sense of playfulness into a sophisticated space,” he says.

Rayman Boozer’s home, featuring an Apartment 48 tiger rug.

Steven Loloi, co-principal at Loloi, agrees. Speaking of Loloi’s Roam collection that launched last month and features cheetahs, zebras, elephants, and giraffes in neutral colors, he highlights the surprising versatility of the pieces, which he says can fit just as nicely in a bedroom or living room as in a lounge or den. “I think we’re seeing people become more confident in their design choices and a little less concerned with playing it safe,” he says. “Why not have a leopard or zebra in your living room?”

It’s worth noting that these rugs aren’t for everyone, and some designers avoid any type of animal rug because of the hunting culture they reference. Others, though, embrace them as a way to reimagine humanity’s relationship to animals and commit to living better by them.

Rajaram's Bahaar rug does just that with its contemporary expression of 'shikargahs,' the enclosed forests where kings hunted at leisure, which are celebrated in Iranian and Mughal design. “Instead of being chased, the animals are in harmony with each other, frolicking freely in the forest. It’s a celebration of coexistence rather than conquest,” she says. The Charlap Hyman & Herrero x Patterson Flynn collection had a similar ambition: “Our Tigre and Oso nod to traditional hide floor coverings; they give you the drama of the trophy rug without the trophy,” notes Marshall.

On the surface, the return of these animal-forward rugs might have looked like a change in aesthetics, but it’s really much more anthropological. “We have always gravitated toward pieces with animals, and even in modern production, history is repeating itself,” says Nazmiyal. Some 2,500 years after their first spotting, these animal-clad rugs are back home.

#4742. The Best Fall Skincare Routine, According to Dermatologists

Your cold-weather glow starts with these expert-approved tweaks.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I finally pulled my favorite fuzzy black jacket out of my closet for long strolls around New York City. Many of the leaves in Central Park are turning a gorgeous burnt-orange hue, and hot apple cider is readily available at local cafes and farmers' markets. But like clockwork every fall since moving to New York from Florida, my skin has been feeling dry, tight, and a little itchy. My complexion is also a little flushed after cleansing, which isn’t the norm during the spring and summer.

Turns out that I’m not alone. Dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD, says her patients often experience rough or flaky patches, dullness, and increased sensitivity to products they previously tolerated well after cleansing this time of year. They also notice tightness, itching, and products that suddenly sting. Sure, cranking up my pretty pink Canopy humidifier can help a little, but after talking with dermatologists, it’s officially time to upgrade my skincare routine for fall.

The good news: We don’t need to replace our entire routine this fall. Dermatologists share their ideal morning and night skincare tweaks. Plus, they reveal how to safely exfoliate dry, flaky skin, and weigh in on using retinoids. The best part? Many of their suggestions are drugstore staples from brands like Cetaphil and La Roche-Posay.

“A healthy barrier does not require a ten-product supporting cast,” says Dr. Gohara. You really only need a few key items—and you may even have them in your home already. Here’s a roundup of dermatologist-recommended products the pros agree are worthy of a spot in your skincare routine. I also included my favorite face sunscreen for the morning and eye cream for twice daily use.

Dr. Nazarian swears by this Cetaphil option and calls it her top cleanser because it's, well, super gentle. She highlights the trifecta of glycerin, niacinamide, and panthenol, as a major win for your skincare game. Notably, glycerin is a humectant to hold onto moisture.

Aveeno Positively Radiant Vitamin C Serum

“Glow with a built-in comfort crew,” says Dr. Gohara about this Skincare Award-winning face serum. “Vitamin C is a proven skin-brightening, collagen-boosting powerhouse. The only problem: it’s known to be irritating on sensitive skin. Aveeno has solved for that here, adding a calming concoction of niacinamide and the brand’s famed oat complex,” says beauty director Brian Underwood.

We’ve previously named this the best overall hyaluronic acid serum and Dr. Nazarian agrees. She appreciates that it boasts multiple forms of hyaluronic acid to enhance hydration, adding that it’s a great serum for layering with other products in your routine.

You can slather this budget-friendly moisturizer on your face and body. It earned snaps from Dr. Gohara, who points to the combination of glycerin to attract water and ceramides to support the skin barrier.

Pro tip from Dr. Gohara: Whether you use a lotion or a face cream, apply it to slightly damp skin.

For extra dryness, layer SkinMedica Barrier Calming Cream on top, advises Dr. Gohara. “Just as you double up on clothes, you can double up on moisturizer. Hydration first, a protective outer layer second,” she says. And that’s exactly what the Barrier Calming Cream does. It contains a nourishing blend of moisturizing glycerin, niacinamide to minimize skin inflammation, and calming oat kernel extract.

The experts I chatted with say eye cream is a totally optional step. You can technically get away with just using a plain face moisturizer under your eyes, says Dr. Nazarian. However, since the undereye skin is thinner and prone to dryness during colder months, a separate eye cream can be helpful for dealing with dryness, fine lines, or crepiness.

Neocutis combines human growth factors with a proprietary blend of peptides to target fine lines, wrinkles, puffiness, and dark circles. After about two weeks, I noticed my undereye area was a little more luminous.

Isdin Eryfotona Actinica Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50+

You shouldn’t retire your sunscreen in the fall, argues Dr. Gohara. A broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher sunscreen is a daily staple. My all-time favorite one is the Isdin Eryfotona Ageless—it’s a tinted mineral sunscreen that doesn’t leave a ghastly finish on my face. It contains plankton-derived DNA Repairsomes, which Isdin says help repair existing sun damage. The formulation is lightweight and absorbs quickly and it’s even water-resistant for active lifestyles.

SkinMedica HA5 Hydra Collagen Facial Mist

Spritz your skin with this spray whenever your complexion needs extra TLC. Dr. Gohara calls this your skin’s “hydration intermission.” It moisturizes and helps keep water in, and layers beautifully over makeup.

Before you go to bed and watch TV, you’ll want to do your skincare routine. You can use pretty much everything from your morning routine.

This creamy cleanser is great for seasonal dryness.

Pro tip from Dr. Garshick: Avoid washing with very hot water since it can contribute to dryness. If you have very sensitive skin, consider splashing your face with water instead of cleansing twice daily, she says.

"This eye cream is rich without being heavy so it won’t leave skin with an oily finish,” says dermatologist Joshua Zeichner, MD, in our 2020 Skincare Awards. He loves that it can “help strengthen the skin and improve texture and fine lines—no irritation in sight."

Lock in hydration with this lightweight face serum that doesn’t feel overly tacky on your skin.

SkinMedica makes a slew of impressive products, including a recent 2026 Skincare Award win for the Exfoliating Pads. However, when you’re shopping for a moisturizer for fall, consider this investment-worthy pick. While pricey, you only need a few small dabs of cream all over your face.

Dr. Nazarian suggests Dermal Repair Cream to anyone who wants to use a retinoid product in the fall. “It’s incredibly hydrating and calming—and uses a form of hyaluronic acid combined with vitamins C and E for skin hydration and environmental defense along with a gentle form of retinoid,” she says. Just be sure to gradually introduce it into your routine.

In the fall, it’s all about hydration. Both Dr. Garshick and Dr. Nazarian suggest humectants such as glycerin and hyaluronic acid to attract water, plus skin barrier-supporting ingredients such as ceramides. You might also benefit from slathering on a richer cream packed with fatty acids, shea butter, or squalane if your skin is very dry.

Yes, you can exfoliate in the fall, but only occasionally. TBH, the frequency varies based on your specific needs and the product you’re using. But you can probably start with once a week or even every two weeks if you have more sensitive skin. You should also avoid scrubbing irritated skin and not exfoliate the same night you use a retinoid while building tolerance. “Flakes are not an invitation to scrub harder,” says Dr. Gohara. “You are polishing skin, not refinishing furniture.” Also, don't be afraid to pause exfoliating if your skin ever feels uncomfy. You can just use your classic face moisturizer until your skin feels comfortable again, adds Dr. Gohara.

Look, just because it’s overcast and chilly out doesn’t mean you should skip wearing sunscreen in the fall. And don’t just take my word for it: “Your sweaters have seasonal employment; your sunscreen works year-round,” says Dr. Gohara. That means you should wear a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher on your exposed skin, including your ears, neck, and hands. Follow your sunscreen label for specific reapplication tips, but typically, you can reapply at least every two hours and after sweating or swimming, according to the American Academy of Dermatology.

The experts I spoke with say you can use a retinoid year-round if your skin can tolerate it and if you diligently reapply sunscreen. However, fall is a convenient time to add a retinoid—such as retinol, retinal, tretinoin, or adapalene—into your routine. Regardless of which type of retinoid you select, start using it gradually. Dr. Garshick says two or three times a week is a good jumping off point, then you can increase frequency as tolerated.
